name: Abdominal hysterectomy (remove uterus)
description: A surgical procedure to remove the uterus, and possibly the ovaries, through the abdomen. There are many reasons the uterus needs to be removed including: tumors, chronic pain, prolapse, and persistent bleeding.
common_complications: Excessive bleeding and infection after the surgery are the most common complications. Other problems may include the development of blood clots, chronic abdominal pain, damage to other pelvic organs, and earlier menopause. The most common pelvic organ damaged is the ureter (the tube that carries urine from the kidney to the bladder). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia including allergic reactions.

name: Abdominal ultrasound (imaging procedure)
description: A diagnostic imaging procedure. The ultrasound device is pressed against the abdomen, and sound waves from the device bounce off tissues and create echoes. The pictures can be used to diagnose abnormalities of the liver, gallbladder, spleen, appendix, pancreas, kidneys, blood vessels and other conditions. Also known as transabdominal ultrasound.
common_complications: There are no complications with an ultrasound procedure.

name: ACTH stimulation test (evaluate adrenal glands)
description: A medical test that evaluates the functioning of the adrenal glands. A hormone called ACTH (adrenocorticotropic hormone) is injected into the blood stream and the amount of cortisol produced is measured. The test can help diagnose adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease).
common_complications: Complications are rarely seen. Side effects may include rash, fainting, headache, blurry vision, swelling, dizziness, palpitations, shortness of breath.

name: Adenoidectomy (removal of adenoids)
description: A surgical procedure to remove the adenoids (lymph tissue in the back of the mouth and throat). Indications include a history of adenoids that are enlarged or frequently infected, causing ear infections, sinus infections or sleep disorders.
common_complications: Nasal stuffiness is common. Other less common complications include bleeding and infection from the surgery site. Call the doctor if the bleeding is brisk, for a persistent fever or severe pain.  The surgery can result in post-operative pain or infection.  Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia including allergic reactions.

name: Amniocentesis (sample amniotic fluid)
description: A diagnostic procedure to sample the amniotic fluid surrounding a fetus, most commonly used to detect birth defects during pregnancy. A needle is inserted through the abdomen and uterus and then into the amniotic sac. An ultrasound is used to direct the needle away from the fetus. The procedure is usually done between the 16th and 20th week of pregnancy.
common_complications: Pain, infection and bleeding can occur. Infection of the amniotic fluid can result in preterm labor and miscarriage. Direct injury to the fetus can also occur. The complication rate is low.

name: Amputation (remove limb)
description: A surgical procedure to remove part or all of a limb or appendage. Some reasons for amputation include: peripheral artery disease, long standing diabetes, severe traumatic damage to the limb, cancer and persistent infection despite antibiotics.
common_complications: Infection and pain. Rarely a patient continues to feel pain in the removed limb (phantom limb pain).  The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia including allergic reactions and very rarely a heart attack or stroke.

name: Anastomosis (connect two structures)
description: A procedure to attach viable tubular structures in the body after the diseased portion has been surgically removed, such as blood vessels or loops of intestine.
common_complications: Any major surgery can result in infection, pain and the development of blood clots in the legs after surgery. Other problems can occur when there is leaking of the surgical connection. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia including allergic reactions and very rarely a heart attack or stroke.

name: Anesthesia (make numb or unconscious)
description: A method of providing partial or complete loss of sensation in part or all of the body, most often using drugs called anesthetics.  Its commonly used to block the pain of surgery. Anesthesia can be local (such as numbing a tooth for drilling a cavity), regional (numbing an entire arm for an operation) or general (being put to sleep).
common_complications: A patients risk of anesthesia increases with age and with other co-existing medical problems. The most serious complications are associated with general anesthesia and can result in breathing problems, lung infections from aspiration (breathing in stomach contents into the lungs) and/or death.  Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia including allergic reactions and very rarely a heart attack or stroke.

name: Angiography (x-ray blood vessels)
description: A diagnostic procedure to x-ray blood vessels. Dye is injected into the vessel using a catheter which allows the vascular structures to be visualized. This procedure can identify blockages and other problems interfering with the flow of blood.
common_complications: The vessel being examined can be damaged and torn resulting in bleeding or loss of the vessel. A blood clot can develop in the vessel after the procedure. Patients can have allergic reactions to the dye resulting in rash, swelling, shortness of breath and very rarely shock. The contrast dye can injure the kidneys, especially if the person has underlying kidney disease.

name: Angioplasty (open blocked artery)
description: A procedure, usually using a small inflatable balloon, to open clogged arteries. Many times a stent or small tube is placed in the vessel to keep it open.
common_complications: The procedure can result in pain and/or infection. The artery can be torn or damaged when the balloon is inflated. A blood clot can occur in the vessel after the catheter is removed. Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the medications given during the procedure.

name: Antibody therapy for cancer (kill tumor cells)
description: A medical therapy using substances to kill specific tumor cells or stimulate the immune system to kill tumor cells.
common_complications: Some normal cells can be killed in the process.

name: Appendectomy (remove appendix)
description: A surgical procedure to remove the appendix. This procedure can be done by opening the abdomen or with small incisions, using special instruments and a camera called a laparoscope (laparoscopic appendectomy).
common_complications: Any major surgery can result in infection, pain, and the development of blood clots in the legs or lungs after surgery. Appendectomy can result in an intra-abdominal infection, intestinal obstruction, or damage to other organs in the abdomen. Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Arteriography (x-ray arteries)
description: A diagnostic procedure to x-ray arteries. Dye is injected into the artery using a catheter or small tube which allows the vascular structures to be visualized.
common_complications: The vessel being examined can be damaged and torn resulting in bleeding or loss of the vessel. A blood clot can develop in the vessel after the procedure. Patients can have allergic reactions to the dye resulting in rash, swelling, shortness of breath and very rarely shock. The contrast dye can injure the kidneys, especially if the person has underlying kidney disease.

name: Arthroscopy (joint examination using camera)
description: A surgical procedure used by orthopedic surgeons to diagnose and treat problems inside a joint. An instrument with a small camera is inserted into the joint to determine what structures are damaged. Many times the surgeon can repair the injuries at the same time.
common_complications: Infection of the joint requiring additional surgeries and antibiotics. Damage to the joint from insertion of the instrument. A blood clot can develop after surgery.

name: Aspiration (remove fluid with a needle)
description: A procedure that uses a needle and syringe to draw out fluid. The fluid can be taken from a cyst, joint, abscess or any other collection of fluid in the body.
common_complications: Infection or pain at the site of the needle insertion.

name: Autologous bone marrow transplantation (use patient's own bone marrow)
description: A procedure in which bone marrow is removed from a patient, stored, and then given back to the patient after treatment.
common_complications: Bone marrow transplantation is a complex procedure with potentially serious consequences. Complications include: low blood cell counts leading to infection and/or anemia, breathing problems, and damage to the liver or heart.

name: Balloon angioplasty (open artery)
description: A procedure to open clogged or blocked arteries usually involving the heart but can be used in other arteries. A catheter is positioned in the narrowed artery, with a tiny balloon at its tip. The balloon is then inflated and deflated sequentially to stretch or break open the narrowing. This improves the size of the opening and passage for blood flow. Many times a stent (small tube) will be placed in the artery afterward to keep it from closing.
common_complications: The vessel can be torn (dissection) or damaged causing bleeding or loss of the vessel. At times the damage requires an emergent bypass of the artery. Infection and pain at the insertion site. Dilation of the vessel can cause a pseudo-aneurysm.  The procedure can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the medications given during the procedure.

name: Barium enema (lower GI series, x-ray colon)
description: A diagnostic procedure to x-ray the rectum and large intestine. The x-rays are taken after the person is given an enema with a barium containing solutions, which coats the inner lining of the rectum and large intestine.
common_complications: Occasionally constipation occurs. Rarely perforation of the rectum or colon occurs.

name: Barium swallow (upper GI series, x-ray upper GI tract)
description: A diagnostic procedure to take x-ray pictures of the esophagus as a person swallows a barium containing solution, which coats the inner lining of the esophagus. The barium solution moves into the stomach and small intestine. X-rays are taken of these structures also. This test is also called an esophagram and can help diagnose the causes of pain and swallowing difficulties.
common_complications: Complications are very rare.

name: Biological therapy (immune system modification to treat disease)
description: A medical therapy that alters the immune system. Depending on the specific type of therapy, it may either stimulate or suppress the immune system. It is used most often to treat cancer and autoimmune diseases.
common_complications: Complications can be mild such as rash, itching and flu-like symptoms to severe such as very low blood pressure and increased risk of infection.

name: Biopsy (remove cells or tissue)
description: A procedure to remove cells or tissue for examination under a microscope. The type of biopsy depends on the size and location of the area to be biopsied. It may be done with a skinny needle to suck out cells, a bigger needle that takes a core of tissue, or surgical removal of part or all of the tissue (excisional biopsy).
common_complications: Infection at the biopsy site. Damage of surrounding tissue or underlying nerves or blood vessels.

name: Blepharoplasty (eye lift)
description: A cosmetic surgical procedure to remove excess fat and skin from the upper and lower eyelids.
common_complications: Infection, bleeding, and an unsatisfactory cosmetic result are the major risks. Rarely, double vision, loss of vision, and/or damage to the tear ducts can occur.

name: Blood transfusion (replace blood)
description: A medical procedure to administer blood or blood products into the blood stream, usually for a low blood count from bleeding or anemia.
common_complications: Even after cross matching of blood reactions can occur. Severe reactions cause fever, shortness of breath, chest pain and rarely shock. Milder reactions include hives, itching and a feeling of uneasiness. Infection is another rare complication.

name: Bone density scan (test of bone strength)
description: A diagnostic procedure to measure the density or calcium content of a patient's bones. The bone density indicates the strength of the bones, and the risk or level of osteoporosis. Lower levels of bone density may lead to more fractures.
common_complications: A non-invasive test with no expected complications.

name: Bone marrow biopsy (bone marrow sample)
description: A procedure to remove a sample of tissue from the bone marrow with a needle for examination under a microscope. It is usually done in the back part of the pelvic bone. The procedure is done to help diagnose the specific cause of anemia and other blood cell diseases or determine if cancer is present.
common_complications: Pain at the biopsy site. Complications are rare.

name: Bone marrow transplantation (replace bone marrow)
description: A procedure to replace bone marrow. Can be used following treatment for certain cancers in which the bone marrow has been destroyed by anticancer drugs or radiation. It can also be used as a treatment for certain types of anemia's, such as sickle cell and aplastic anemia. Transplantation may be autologous (an individual's own marrow saved before treatment), allogeneic (marrow donated by someone else), or syngeneic (marrow donated by an identical twin).
common_complications: Bone marrow transplantation is a complex procedure with potentially serious consequences. Complications include: low blood cell counts leading to infection and/or anemia, breathing problems, and damage to the liver or heart.

name: Bone scan (image of bones)
description: A diagnostic test to create images of bones for evaluation. Radioactive material is injected into a blood vessel and collects in the bones. It is then detected by a scanner. A bone scan detects increased metabolic activity and can be used to diagnose bone infections, fractures or cancer.
common_complications: Complications are very rare but include an allergic reaction.

name: Botox injections (skin injection of small amount of toxin)
description: A procedure involving the injection of botulinum toxin into certain muscles to treat some medical disorders, such as severe muscle spasticity and chronic migraine, or for cosmetic purposes.
common_complications: The most common complications are bruising and unwanted cosmetic results.

name: Brachytherapy (cancer treatment)
description: A procedure in which radioactive material is implanted in the body to provide localized radiation therapy. It is also called internal radiation, implant radiation, or interstitial radiation therapy. It is most commonly used to treat prostate, breast, cervical, and skin cancer.
common_complications: Infection and pain are initial possible complications. Long term problems are associated with the damage to the surrounding tissue.

name: Breast augmentation or enlargement (implant)
description: A surgical procedure to increase the size of the breast with an implant placed behind the breast in the soft tissue or muscle layers.
common_complications: Surgery can result in infection, pain, and the development of blood clots in the legs or lungs after surgery. An unsatisfactory result is always a possibility with cosmetic or reconstructive surgery. Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Breast implant removal
description: A surgical procedure to remove previously placed breast implants. The three most common reasons for breast implant removal are change of size and shape, implant leakage or rupture, and capsular contracture.
common_complications: Surgery can result in infection, pain, and the development of blood clots in the legs or lungs after surgery. An unsatisfactory result is always a possibility with cosmetic or reconstructive surgery.  Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Breast lift (mastopexy)
description: A surgical procedure to lift the breast by raising the nipple and areola to a higher level, which can be performed with various different incisions depending upon the degree of sagging. Occasionally, a breast implant is used to improve the size, shape, firmness and projection of the breast in conjunction with the breast lift.
common_complications: Surgery can result in infection, pain, and the development of blood clots in the legs or lungs after surgery. An unsatisfactory result is always a possibility with cosmetic or reconstructive surgery. Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Breast reduction (reduction mammaplasty)
description: A surgical procedure involving the removal of excess skin, fat, and glandular tissue of the breast. It also commonly requires a reduction in the size of the areola (nipple), since it is usually stretched out from the constant weight of the breast. The procedure is usually performed to alleviate discomfort, to achieve a breast size in proportion with the patient's body, for cosmetic reasons, or to improve performance in sport activities.
common_complications: Surgery can result in infection, pain, and the development of blood clots in the legs or lungs after surgery. An unsatisfactory result is always a possibility with cosmetic or reconstructive surgery. Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Breast conserving surgery (removal of part of the breast)
description: This procedure is also called breast-sparing surgery and involves removing only the portion of the breast containing cancer and the immediate surrounding breast tissue. Lumpectomy only removes the lump with a minimal border of normal appearing breast tissue. Partial or segmental mastectomy involves removal of a larger amount of breast tissue than lumpectomy. Quadrantectomy removes one fourth of the breast.
common_complications: Surgery can result in infection, pain, and the development of blood clots in the legs or lungs after surgery.  Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Bronchoscopy (camera images of lung)
description: A medical procedure that uses a bronchoscope, a flexible tube with a small light and camera, to examine the airways of the lung. This procedure is used to diagnose problems in the lungs by directly viewing the airways and taking samples or biopsies. It can help diagnose the specific cause of lung symptoms and/or chest x-ray abnormalities.
common_complications: Potential complications include allergic reactions to the sedation medications, aspiration of stomach contents, and injury to the mouth, throat, or lungs.

name: Bypass (create new pathway for blood)
description: A surgical procedure usually involving the creation of a new pathway for blood flow. A cardiac bypass creates new blood flow to the heart.
common_complications: Surgery can result in infection, pain, and the development of blood clots in the legs or lungs after surgery. The bypassed arteries can be damaged and the organ they supply can be damaged. Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia including allergic reactions and very rarely a heart attack or stroke.

name: Capsule endoscopy (camera in a swallowed capsule)
description: A diagnostic procedure involving swallowing a capsule containing a tiny camera. It takes pictures as it glides through the small intestine and is then excreted from the body. It can help diagnose polyps, cancer, or causes of bleeding and anemia.
common_complications: Complications are rare.

name: Cardiac catheterization (heart artery pictures)
description: A diagnostic procedure used to explore the coronary arteries, involving use of a catheter entering the body from an artery in the leg, and passed into the arteries of the heart. It can help diagnose heart disease and coronary artery blockages.
common_complications: The vessel being examined can be damaged and torn resulting in bleeding or loss of the vessel. A blood clot can develop in the vessel after the procedure. Patients can have allergic reactions to the dye resulting in rash, swelling, shortness of breath and very low blood pressure. The contrast dye can injure the kidneys, especially if the person has underlying kidney disease. The site of insertion can become infected.

name: Cardioversion (convert to normal heart rhythm)
description: A medical procedure using electrical currents to restore the heart beat to a normal rhythm when a patient has a persistent irregular heart rhythm or a new arrhythmia. Atrial fibrillation, atrial flutter, supra-ventricular tachycardia and ventricular tachycardia are the most common abnormal rhythms to be treated with cardioversion.
common_complications: Sedation given for the procedure can result in allergic reactions or breathing problems. Residual soreness chest soreness is the most common side effects. Very rarely, the electrical current delivered can cause a very slow or fast heart rate.

name: Carotid endarterectomy (unclog carotid artery)
description: A surgical procedure to unclog the carotid artery in the neck in the hope of preventing strokes.
common_complications: Surgery can result in infection, pain, and the development of blood clots in the legs or lungs after surgery. The carotid artery can be damaged resulting in life threatening bleeding or a stroke.  Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia including allergic reactions and very rarely a heart attack or stroke.

name: Carotid ultrasound exam (neck artery imaging)
description: A diagnostic procedure to examine the arteries in the neck for narrowing or stenosis. Sound waves are used to evaluate the inside of vessel and the blood flow through the artery. The amount of narrowing determines the risk of future strokes.
common_complications: None unless too much pressure is applied to the carotid arteries during the ultrasound exam.

name: Castration (removal of testicles or ovaries)
description: A procedure or therapy that removes the functioning of the testicles or ovaries. There are multiple methods including surgical removal, radiation and/or drugs. Drugs suppress the hormone production of the testicles and ovaries and this is called medical castration.
common_complications: Surgery can result in infection, pain, and the development of blood clots in the legs or lungs after surgery. The loss of hormones from the removal of the testicles or ovaries can cause hot flashes and other symptoms similar to low testosterone in men and menopause in woman. Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Cataract surgery (remove cataract from eye)
description: A surgical procedure to remove or dissolve the clouded lens of the eye formed as a result of a cataract. In most cases a permanent intraocular lens (IOL) is inserted.
common_complications: Decrease vision and loss of vision are the most serious complications.

name: Catheterization (insertion of hollow tube)
description: A procedure involving the insertion of a catheter into the body. Many things can be catheterized for different reasons, including the bladder, the arteries, or the veins.
common_complications: The complications depend on the area of the body being catheterized.

name: Cauterization (stops bleeding)
description: A surgical procedure to destroy tissue with a hot instrument, an electrical current, or a caustic substance. It is commonly used in surgery to stop bleeding.
common_complications: Pain, infection and local tissue destruction are the main complications.

name: Celioscopy (camera exam of abdominal cavity)
description: A surgical procedure that uses a small surgical tube with a camera called a laparoscope. The laparoscope is inserted into the abdomen and is used to examine and treat the abdominal and pelvic organs. This procedure can be used to treat many conditions including appendicitis, pelvic inflammatory disease, ectopic pregnancy and ovarian cyst.
common_complications: Any surgery can result in infection, pain, and the development of blood clots in the legs or lungs after surgery. Abdominal surgery can result in an intra-abdominal infection, intestinal obstruction, or damage to other organs in the abdomen.

name: Central line placement (place large IV into a vein)
description: A procedure to place a large bore intravenous catheter into the subclavian, internal jugular, or femoral vein for IV access, blood draw, and medication delivery. The procedure may be done with the help of an ultrasound.
common_complications: Infection at the insertion site, damage to the blood vessel, and a blood clot in the vessel are the most common complications.

name: Cerebral angiography (brain blood vessel images)
description: A diagnostic procedure to x-ray the blood vessels of the brain using contrast injected into the blood stream. It can be used to diagnose problems of the brain and brainstem such as aneurysm.
common_complications: The vessel being examined can be damaged and torn resulting in bleeding or loss of the vessel. A blood clot can develop in the vessel after the procedure rarely resulting in a stroke. Patients can have allergic reactions to the dye resulting in rash, swelling, shortness of breath and shock. The contrast dye can injure the kidneys, especially if the person has underlying kidney disease.

name: Cesarean section (surgical delivery of baby)
description: A surgical procedure that removes the baby from a mother's uterus through an incision in her abdomen. A cesarean section is also called a C-section and is performed when the mother cannot deliver the baby through the vagina or if the baby is in distress.
common_complications: Any major surgery can result in infection, pain, and the development of blood clots in the legs or lungs after surgery. A C-section can result in an intra-abdominal infection, intestinal obstruction, or damage to the uterus or other organs in the pelvis.

name: Chemical peel (improve texture of facial skin)
description: A medical procedure using a chemical solution that removes damaged skin. The procedure is performed to smooth out the texture of the facial skin and is useful for patients with excessive wrinkles or blemishes. The most commonly used chemicals are alpha hydroxy acids, phenol and trichloroacetic acid.
common_complications: Complications range from minor skin irritation to permanent scarring. Rarely more serious allergic reactions to the chemicals can occur.

name: Chemoembolization (treatment for liver cancer)
description: A procedure that involves administering anticancer drugs directly into an artery that supplies blood to a tumor. This is immediately followed by injection of a substance that causes a blockage in the same artery. This permits a higher concentration of drug to be in contact with the tumor for a longer period of time.
common_complications: The embolization chemical can travel to the wrong area resulting in the destruction of healthy tissue. The most serious risks are infection and massive damage to the liver.

name: Chemotherapy (cancer treatment)
description: The use of drugs to treat cancer. These drugs generally kill tumor cells preferentially over normal cells.
common_complications: Hair loss, nausea, vomiting and diarrhea are common. At times a patient's bone marrow is damaged resulting in low red blood cells (anemia), easy bleeding from low platelets (thrombocytopenia), and increased infections from a low white blood cell count (neutropenia).

name: Chin implant (change shape of chin)
description: A surgical procedure to correct an abnormally shaped chin. A surgical incision is made in the skin or inside the mouth and a silicone implant is placed.
common_complications: Surgery can result in pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). A poor cosmetic result is also a risk.  Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Cholecystectomy (remove gallbladder)
description: A surgical procedure to remove the gallbladder. The most common reason for removing a gallbladder is gallstones causing symptoms or an infection of the gallbladder. The gallbladder can be removed through a large incision (open) or through a laparoscope (laparoscopically).
common_complications: Surgery can result in pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Damage and leaking of a bile duct can result in a fluid collection and abscess (collection of pus). At times a stone can be left behind (retained stone) in one of the bile ducts.  Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Chorionic villus sampling or CVS (detects birth defects)
description: A diagnostic procedure used during pregnancy to diagnose birth defects. A small sample of placental cells called the chorionic villi is obtained by inserting a small tube through the pregnant patient's vagina and cervix into the uterus (transcervical approach). The procedure can also be performed by passing the tube through the abdominal wall into the uterus and placenta (transabdominal approach). There is a slight increased risk of losing the baby with the transcervical approach. An ultrasound sound is used to help guide the tube in both techniques. CVS can test for conditions such as Down syndrome, Tay Sachs disease, and cystic fibrosis. It is usually performed during the first trimester of pregnancy.
common_complications: Miscarriage (loss of the pregnancy) and bleeding.

name: Colectomy (remove large intestine)
description: A surgical procedure to remove the colon or a portion of the colon. This procedure can be performed through an incision in the abdomen (open colectomy) or by using a laparoscope. A laparoscope is a small lighted surgical tube attached to a camera that is inserted through a small incision in the abdomen. Colectomies are performed for the following medical conditions: cancer, inflammatory bowel disease, diverticulitis, and bowel obstructions.
common_complications: Surgery can result in pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) and lungs (pulmonary embolus). Leaking of intestinal contents into the abdomen and damage to other organs in the abdomen can also occur. With time scar tissue can develop causing adhesions and blockages of the bowel (intestinal obstruction). Total colectomy may require a colostomy. Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia including allergic reactions and very rarely a heart attack or stroke.

name: Colonoscopy (large intestine camera exam)
description: A procedure that uses a small lighted tube with a camera to examine the inside of the colon. It is performed most often to screen for polyps and colon cancer. The tube is inserted through the anus and if abnormalities are seen in the colon they can be biopsied or removed at the same time. This procedure is also used to help diagnose and stage inflammatory bowel disease.
common_complications: Abdominal bloating, pain, and mild rectal bleeding can occur. Perforation of the colon with spilling of intestinal contents into the abdomen and infection is the most serious complication.

name: Colostomy (colon attached to abdominal wall)
description: A surgical procedure that involves connecting the large intestine (colon) to the outside of the abdomen. This opening of the colon is called a stoma. Colostomies are sometimes necessary in the following medical conditions: cancer, traumatic injuries, infections, and other serious diseases of the large intestine. For an excellent video on how to change a colostomy bag go to: http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=31Q2G2D-EW8&feature=youtube_gdata_player
common_complications: Surgery can result in pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). A hernia or weakening of tissue around the opening may occur.  Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia.

name: Colposcopy (examination of cervix)
description: A diagnostic procedure to examine the vagina and cervix using a colposcope which magnifies the lining of the vagina and cervix. It is used to help identify specific areas that may be precancerous or cancerous. Its often done after a woman has an abnormal Pap smear.
common_complications: Vaginal bleeding. Other complications are rare.

name: Combination chemotherapy (cancer treatment)
description: A treatment using more than one anticancer drug. These drugs generally kill cancer cells preferentially over normal cells.
common_complications: The loss of one's hair, nausea, vomiting and diarrhea are common. At times a patient's bone marrow is damaged resulting in low red blood cells (anemia), easy bleeding from low platelets (thrombocytopenia), and increased infections from a low white blood cell count (neutropenia).

name: Complete hysterectomy (remove uterus)
description: A surgical procedure to remove the entire uterus, often including the entire cervix. The surgery can be done through the vagina (vaginal hysterectomy) or through the abdomen (abdominal hysterectomy).
common_complications: Surgery can result in pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Damage to the other organs including the intestine or ureter (tube connecting kidney to bladder).  Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Computed tomography (CT or CAT scan)
description: A series of x-rays of areas inside the body processed by a computer to provide very detailed pictures. Also called CT or CAT scan.
common_complications: CT scans require radiation. Multiple exposures to radiation increase the risk of cancer later in life. At times intravenous contrast is given with a CT scan. The contrast used may cause kidney injury. Some patients can be allergic to the contrast resulting in a rash to life-threatening swelling and low blood pressure.

name: Cone biopsy (sample of cervix)
description: A surgical procedure to remove a cone-shaped piece of tissue from the cervix and cervical canal. Cone biopsy, also called conization, may be used to diagnose or treat a cervical condition such as cancer.
common_complications: Vaginal bleeding is the most common complication. Rarely the bleeding can be severe requiring an immediate hysterectomy. Reactions to the anesthesia and infection can also occur. The cervix can be damaged causing scarring and making future pregnancies difficult.

name: Coronary angiogram (x-ray heart arteries)
description: A procedure to x-ray blood vessels in the heart. Dye is injected into the vessel using a catheter which allows the blood vessels to be visualized. This procedure can identify blockages and other problems interfering with the flow of blood.
common_complications: Damage to the blood vessels of the heart or leg, rarely requiring immediate surgery. The contrast used may cause kidney injury. Some patients can be allergic to the contrast causing a reaction from a rash to life threatening swelling or drop in blood pressure.

name: Coronary angioplasty (unclog heart arteries)
description: A medical procedure used to restore flow through narrowed or blocked arteries that supply blood to the heart muscle. The artery is opened with a balloon, often followed by placement of a tube (stent) to help prevent future blockage.
common_complications: Damage to the blood vessels of the heart or leg, rarely requiring immediate surgery. The contrast used may cause kidney injury. Some patients can be allergic to the contrast causing a reaction from a rash to life threatening swelling or drop in blood pressure.

name: Coronary artery bypass operation (bypass blocked heart artery)
description: A surgical procedure to bypass the blockage and restore blood flow in one or more coronary (heart) arteries. For each bypassed artery, a blood vessel, taken from the leg, arm or chest, is grafted into the artery above and beyond the blockage. By restoring blood flow to the heart, it can help prevent heart attacks and improve heart function.
common_complications: The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection and/or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Risks also include bad reactions to general anesthesia, heart attack, stroke and death.

name: Craniotomy (hole in the head)
description: A surgical procedure where an opening is made in the skull for examining and treating brain disorders including benign and cancerous tumors,  aneurysms, and blood collections in between the skull and brain.
common_complications: Surgery can result in pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Other complications include: stroke, seizures, and brain bleeding. There is a small risk permanent brain damage. Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia.

name: Cryosurgery (freeze tissue)
description: A surgical procedure using cold temperatures to freeze and destroy abnormal tissues.
common_complications: Bleeding, blistering, swelling, pain and infection.

name: Cryotherapy (cold treatment)
description: A procedure that uses cold temperature to treat disease. Another term for cryosurgery.
common_complications: Bleeding, blistering, swelling, pain and infection.

name: CT or CAT scan (computed tomography)
description: A series of x-rays of areas inside the body processed by a computer to provide very detailed pictures. Also called computed tomography.
common_complications: CT scans require radiation. Multiple exposures to radiation increase the risk of cancer later in life. At times intravenous contrast is given with a CT scan. The contrast used may cause kidney injury.Some patients can be allergic to the contrast resulting in a rash to life-threatening swelling and low blood pressure.

name: Curettage (remove tissue)
description: A surgical procedure to remove tissue with a curette, which is a sharp, spoon-shaped instrument.
common_complications: Bleeding, swelling, pain, infection and scarring.

name: Cystectomy (remove bladder)
description: A surgical procedure to remove all or part of the bladder, usually for the treatment of bladder cancer.
common_complications: Surgery can result in pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Injury to other organs in the pelvis can occur resulting in sexual dysfunction, and intestinal damage.  Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia.

name: Cystoscopy (camera examination of the bladder)
description: A procedure to examine the bladder and urethra using a thin, lighted instrument (cystoscope) inserted into the urethra. Reasons for the procedure include unexplained blood in the urine, persistent urinary symptoms, and to rule out bladder cancer.
common_complications: Swelling of the urethra preventing urination requiring a placement of a catheter, urinary tract infection, and very rarely damage to the urethra or bladder, such as bladder perforation.

name: Da Vinci Robotic Surgery (minimally invasive robotic surgery)
description: A surgical procedure assisted by three robotic arms that perform the surgery with a variety of surgical tools. The robotic arms give surgeons more intricate motion and tool control for complex surgeries. The Da Vinci Endoscopic Instrument Control System is used for a variety of surgeries, including general gallbladder and reflux disease surgery, prostate surgery, hysterectomy and heart surgery.
common_complications: Surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Defibrillation (start normal heart rhythm using electricity)
description: A medical procedure using an electronic device to administer an electric shock to the heart, to reestablish a normal heart rhythm.
common_complications: Pain at the site of the defibrillation.

name: Dermabrasion (refinish skin)
description: A surgical procedure that removes thin layers of skin either mechanically or with a laser. Dermabrasion is performed to smooth out the skin and remove small blemishes and scars.
common_complications: Pain, scarring, uneven skin coloration and rarely infection.

name: Dialysis (filter and clean blood)
description: A medical procedure to filter and clean the blood when the kidneys are not functioning.
common_complications: Infection and bleeding from the dialysis site. Low blood pressure and blood chemistry imbalances.

name: Diathermy (cauterization)
description: A procedure using heat to destroy abnormal cells or to control bleeding in surgery using a hot instrument, electrical current, or a caustic substance. It is also called cauterization or electrodiathermy.
common_complications: Pain, infection and excessive local tissue destruction are possible but rarely occur.

name: Digital rectal examination (finger examination of rectum)
description: An examination in which a doctor inserts a lubricated, gloved finger into the rectum to feel for abnormalities, such as enlarged prostate gland or rectal tumor. The stool specimen can be tested for the presence of blood.
common_complications: None.

name: Dilation and curettage (D and C, tissue removal inside uterus)
description: A surgical procedure to dilate the cervix, allowing access to the uterus to scrape the lining with a spoon-shaped instrument called a curette (curettage). Reasons for the procedure include abnormal uterine bleeding and to rule out endometrial cancer.
common_complications: Vaginal bleeding and pain. Rarely perforation of the uterus can occur.

name: Discectomy (remove herniated disk)
description: A surgical procedure to remove part of a herniated disk in the spine. This can relieve some of the pressure on a nerve causing pain in the neck, back or leg.
common_complications: Nerve injury. Any surgery can result in pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia. Surgery may not improve the original symptoms, especially if the only symptom was low back pain.

name: Ductal lavage (collect cells from milk ducts in breast)
description: A procedure to collect cells from milk ducts in the breast using a hair-size catheter inserted into the nipple. Salt water is infused into the duct to help remove cells for the detection of breast cancer.
common_complications: Infection. Perforation of the duct can occur which usually heals on its own.

name: Echocardiography (ultrasound of the heart, echocardiogram)
description: A test using ultrasound to study the heart's position, motion of the walls, and valves. This test can be used in the diagnosis of a number of heart conditions including an enlarged heart, valve disorders, weakened heart muscle and blood clots inside the heart.
common_complications: None.

name: Electrocardiogram (EKG or ECG, recording of heart electricity)
description: A common medical test producing a graphic record of the electrical activity of the heart. This test can help diagnose many heart conditions including abnormal rhythms (arrhythmias), heart attacks, heart failure, and an enlarged heart.
common_complications: None.

name: Electroencephalogram (EEG, recording of brain electricity)
description: A recording of the brain's electrical activity used to help diagnose brain disorders such as epilepsy and brain injury.
common_complications: None.

name: Electron beam computed tomography (Coronary calcium heart scan)
description: A computer generated x-ray measuring calcium buildup in and around the coronary arteries, which may indicate an increased risk of heart disease.
common_complications: Multiple exposures to radiation can increase the risk of cancer later in life.

name: Electronystagmogram (electronystagmography, ENG, inner ear test)
description: A medical test of the vestibular system which is used to help diagnose balance problems. The test involves placing electrodes on the patient's head and measuring electrical impulses associated with eye movements.
common_complications: Rarely nausea that resolves quickly after the test.

name: Embolization (block an artery)
description: A surgical procedure to block an artery using a balloon or coil. Embolization can be done, for example, as a treatment to block the flow of blood to a tumor or a bleeding blood vessel.
common_complications: Infection and pain. At times the wrong vessel can be blocked causing damage to normal adjacent tissue.

name: Endocrine therapy (hormone therapy)
description: A therapy that adds, blocks, or removes hormones for the treatment of many conditions like diabetes, menopause, thyroid conditions, and to stop the growth of certain cancers.
common_complications: Complications depend on the hormones being used and disorder being treated.

name: Endometrial ablation (remove lining of uterus)
description: A surgical procedure that scars the lining of the uterus. It can be used as an alternative to hysterectomy for treatment of excessive menstrual bleeding.
common_complications: Pain, infection, vaginal bleeding, damage to the cervix, and perforation of the uterus.

name: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP)
description: A procedure used to diagnose and treat a variety of gastrointestinal conditions like gallstones and pancreatitis. A flexible tube called an endoscope is inserted in the mouth and passed into the small intestine. The endoscope has a camera and openings for other instruments. The doctor finds the opening of the bile duct and squirts dye into duct as pictures are taken. The dye gets up the duct and also into the pancreatic ducts. If there is a blockage, the doctor may be able to fix it during the procedure.
common_complications: Inflammation of the pancreas (pancreatitis) occurs in 10% of the cases, and severe pancreatitis in 1%. Severe pancreatitis can be serious and even life threatening. Damage to esophagus, stomach or small intestine (duodenum) can also occur but is rare.

name: Endoscopic ultrasound (internal imaging procedure)
description: A medical procedure using an endoscope that is equipped to take close-up ultrasound images of abdominal organs. The endoscope, a flexible tube with a camera, is inserted in the mouth and moved through the esophagus, stomach and first part of the small intestine. During the procedure, the doctor can direct the sound waves to take pictures of hard to reach organs such as the pancreas and bile duct.
common_complications: Possible reaction to medication used for sedation. Damage to esophagus, stomach or small intestine (duodenum) can also occur but is rare.

name: Endoscopy (flexible tube with camera)
description: A medical procedure using a flexible tube with a camera to examine the inside of the esophagus, stomach and first part of the small intestine. Reasons for the procedure include diagnosis and treatment of internal bleeding, ulcers and to help diagnose tumors and other conditions. Small tissue samples (biopsies) can be done through the endoscope.
common_complications: Possible reaction to medication used for sedation. Damage to esophagus, stomach or small intestine (duodenum) can also occur but is rare.

name: Enema (insertion of liquid into rectum)
description: A procedure involving the injection of a liquid through the anus into the large bowel, generally for the treatment of constipation or imaging purposes.
common_complications: Rarely injury to the rectum or large intestine (colon) including perforation can occur.

name: Epidural block (spinal cord anesthesia)
description: A procedure injecting an anesthetic drug into the space between the wall of the spinal canal and the covering of the spinal cord to produce anesthesia below that level of the spinal cord.
common_complications: Infection, pain, bleeding outside the spinal cord, and injury of a nerve can occur. A headache from a spinal fluid leak, called a spinal or postural headache, can also occur.

name: Episiotomy (vaginal incision during childbirth)
description: A surgical procedure, involving an incision between the anus and vagina, used during delivery of a baby to make the vaginal opening larger for a safer delivery. The incision is repaired with stitches after delivery.
common_complications: Bleeding, infection, swelling, defects in wound closure, pain, and possibility of sexual dysfunction.

name: Esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD, camera examination of upper digestive tract)
description: A medical procedure using a flexible tube with a camera to examine the inside of the esophagus, stomach and first part of the small intestine. Reasons for the procedure include diagnosis and treatment of internal bleeding, ulcers and to help diagnose tumors and other conditions. Small tissue samples (biopsies) can be done through the endoscope.
common_complications: Possible reaction to medication used for sedation. Damage to esophagus, stomach or small intestine (duodenum) can also occur but is rare.

name: Esophagoscopy (camera examination of esophagus)
description: A medical procedure using a flexible tube with a camera to examine the inside of the esophagus. It can be helpful in diagnosing cancer, esophageal obstruction, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and other conditions. Doctors can open blockages, stop bleeding or take biopsies of the esophagus through the scope.
common_complications: Possible reaction to medication used for sedation. Damage to the esophagus, including perforation, can also occur but is rare.

name: Esophagram (x-ray images of esophagus)
description: A series of x-rays of the esophagus after the patient drinks a solution containing barium. The barium coats and outlines the esophagus on the x-ray and can be helpful in detecting abnormalities of the esophagus.
common_complications: Rarely patients can choke on the barium causing a lung infection.

name: Excisional biopsy (removal of tissue for evaluation)
description: A surgical procedure in which suspicious tissue is removed for diagnosis and examination under a microscope.
common_complications: Infection and pain. Surrounding tissue and organs can be injured during the excision.

name: External beam radiation (radiation cancer treatment)
description: A therapy that uses a specialized machine to aim high-energy radiation at a cancer. It is also called external radiation.
common_complications: It is not uncommon for surrounding organs to be damaged during the therapy and the complications experienced are dependent on the area receiving the radiation treatment and the amount of radiation delivered.

name: Extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy (noninvasive kidney stone treatment)
description: A medical procedure that uses high-energy shockwaves to break up stones inside the body. It is commonly used for kidney stones that are too big to pass through the urinary tract.
common_complications: Bleeding, infection, blocked ureter, and kidney injury.

name: Facelift (rhytidectomy)
description: A surgical procedure to remove the excess skin of the face and neck region.  The underlying muscles are tightened to achieve the desired result. This can help restore the smoothness and tightness associated with younger skin, as well as to reestablish definition of the neckline.
common_complications: Pain, swelling, nerve injuries, infection, scarring, skin loss, earlobe malformation, and injury to the parotid gland (salivary gland). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Fecal occult blood test (blood in stool)
description: A test to check for blood in the stool, which helps determine if there is intestinal bleeding. It is also used as screening test for possible polyps or cancer.
common_complications: None.

name: Fine needle aspiration (needle biopsy)
description: A procedure to remove fluid and/or cells with a needle for examination under a microscope.  Also known as a needle biopsy.
common_complications: Complications are uncommon, but may include infection, pain, swelling and/or injury to surrounding tissue.

name: Fluoroscopy (x-ray videos of body)
description: A procedure to x-ray the body with an ability to see motion. It is used to visualize bones and internal organs.
common_complications: Multiple exposures to radiation can increase the risk of cancer later in life.

name: Forehead lift (plastic surgery of face)
description: A surgical procedure that can be performed either endoscopically (using a narrow tube with a light and camera at the end) via several small incisions placed within the hairline or through an incision along the length of the hairline. Both approaches involve the removal of any excess muscle which might be contributing to frown lines.
common_complications: Pain, infection, inability to move eyebrows, loss of hair, scar formation, and loss of sensation. Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Fulguration (remove tissue with electric current)
description: A procedure to destroy or remove tissue using an electric current.
common_complications: Infection, bleeding, pain or injury to surrounding tissue.

name: Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI, MRI that measures brain activity)
description: An MRI done while a person is performing different tasks. It is used primarily to help brain surgeons identify specific parts of the brain they want to preserve during surgery, if at all possible.
common_complications: None.

name: Gastrectomy (surgical removal of stomach)
description: A surgical procedure to resect part or all of the stomach. It may be indicated to treat a bleeding ulcer, stomach cancer, or other condition.
common_complications: Any surgery can result in pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Some patients experience dumping syndrome with food entering the small intestine too quickly resulting in: cramping, diarrhea, dizziness, nausea and vomiting,  and sweating. Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia.

name: Gene therapy (use of DNA to treat disease)
description: A treatment that alters or affects a gene in the body.
common_complications: Complications depend on the reason for the gene therapy.

name: General anesthesia (make unconscious)
description: A method to produce complete loss of feeling and awareness to perform a procedure or surgery.
common_complications: In healthy patients serious reactions to general anesthesia are rare. In patients with other illnesses the stress of general anesthesia can result in heart attack and stroke. Other complications include: aspiration (breathing in stomach contents), allergic reactions, and throat pain.

name: Genetic testing (analyze DNA)
description: A procedure to analyze DNA in order to find a genetic alteration. This finding may indicate an increased risk for developing a specific disease or disorder.
common_complications: None.

name: Grading (cancer classification system)
description: A system to classify cancer cells based on the level of abnormal activity and growth they exhibit when viewed close-up under a microscope. A grading system may provide information on how aggressive a cancer may grow or spread within the body. The systems used to grade tumors are different with each type of cancer and usually affect treatment options.
common_complications: None.

name: Hair replacement (transplantation)
description: A surgical procedure where hair transplants are removed from an area where the missing hair will not show, such as the back of the head, just above the neck. This is referred to as the "donor site". The surgeon cuts tiny hair transplantation grafts from this strip of skin, then places them into tiny incisions in the balding area.
common_complications: Numbness, swelling, scarring, poor or no growth of grafts, unnatural appearance of transplanted hair. Any surgery can result in pain or infection.

name: Helical computed tomography (CT scan)
description: A series of x-rays of areas inside the body processed by a computer to provide very detailed pictures. Pictures are taken using a spiral path. Also called CT or CAT scan or Spiral CT scan.
common_complications: CT scans require radiation. Multiple exposures to radiation increase the risk of cancer later in life. If intravenous contrast is used, it can injure the kidneys. Rarely, patients can be allergic to the contrast resulting in a rash to life-threatening swelling and low blood pressure.

name: Hemorrhoidectomy (remove hemorrhoid)
description: A surgical procedure to remove protruding or symptomatic hemorrhoids.
common_complications: Infection, swelling, bleeding and pain.  The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Herniorrhaphy (hernia repair)
description: A surgical procedure to repair a hernia. Hernias can be present in many areas with inguinal, abdominal wall, and the belly button (umbilicus) being the most common types.
common_complications: Injury to the intestine and return of the hernia. Any surgery can result in pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Hormone replacement therapy (post-menopausal hormone therapy or HRT)
description: Hormone therapy contains estrogen with or without progesterone for postmenopausal women or women who have had their ovaries surgically removed. This is done to help treat symptoms, such as hot flashes and vaginal dryness.
common_complications: Increased risk of blood clots. Prolonged use increases the risk of breast cancer. Use in older women may increase the risk of heart attack and stroke.

name: Hyperthermic perfusion (late stage cancer treatment)
description: A medical procedure where warmed anticancer drugs are given to a patient to bathe, or pass through blood vessels of, the tissue or organ containing a tumor.
common_complications: The loss of one's hair, nausea, vomiting and diarrhea are common. At times a patient's bone marrow is damaged resulting in low red blood cells (anemia), easy bleeding from low platelets (thrombocytopenia), and increased infections from a low white blood cell count (neutropenia).

name: Hysterectomy (removal of the uterus)
description: A surgical procedure to remove the uterus. The surgery can be done through the vagina or through the abdomen.
common_complications: Injury to the organs in the pelvis including the bladder, ureter (tube connecting kidney to bladder), intestine, and blood vessels. Any surgery can result in pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus).  Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: ICD implantation (implant to monitor heart rhythm)
description: Surgical implantation of an Implantable Cardioverter Defibrillator which monitors the heart's rhythm and uses an electrical shock to restore a normal heart rhythm. Small incisions are made in the chest where the device is inserted.
common_complications: Complications occur in a small percent of cases and include damage to blood vessels, lung or heart.  Any surgery can result in pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus).  Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Ileostomy (external opening to the small intestine)
description: A surgical procedure to create an opening (stoma) from the ileum (the most distant section of the small intestine) to the outside. An ileostomy allows for waste material to leave the intestinal tract through the skin of the abdominal wall. The waste material collects in a pouch. The procedure is most often done to allow an inflamed or infected colon to heal, or after part or the entire colon is surgically removed.
common_complications: Surgery can result in pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). A hernia or weakening of tissue around the opening may occur. Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Immunization (shots)
description: A medical therapy used to create an immune response. This may result in resistance to a specific disease. This is a common preventive therapy for certain infectious diseases. Immunizations can be administered in infants to adults pending schedules and recommendations set forth by the Centers for Disease Control.
common_complications: Pain and swelling at the injection site. Rarely an infection at the site can occur. Allergic reactions to the immunization can occur.

name: Immunosuppressant (reduce immune system response)
description: A medical treatment that suppresses the body's immune system. This may be an unwanted side effect of chemotherapy to treat cancer or therapy to treat autoimmune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis. Immunosuppressants are also used after organ transplantation to prevent organ rejection. Immunosuppressants decrease the bodys ability to fight infections and can increase the risk of new cancers later on.  Immunosuppression can be done with drugs or radiation.
common_complications: Decreased ability to fight infections and increased risk of certain cancers later on.

name: Immunotherapy (modify immune system)
description: A type of medical therapy to stimulate, enhance or suppress the immune system. These therapies are used to treat certain types of cancer and inflammatory diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis, Crohns disease and multiple sclerosis. Some of the drugs are given to boost red blood cell and white cell counts, after the counts are knocked down by chemotherapy.
common_complications: Side effects vary depending on the type of immunotherapy. For most of them, the greatest risk is the decreased ability to fight infections.

name: Implant radiation (implant radioactive material)
description: A procedure in which radioactive material is implanted in the body to provide localized radiation therapy. It is also called brachytherapy, internal radiation, or interstitial radiation therapy. It is most commonly used to treat prostate, breast, cervical, and skin cancer.
common_complications: Infection and pain are initial possible complications. Long term problems are associated with the damage to the surrounding tissue.

name: Incisional biopsy (remove cells or tissue)
description: A procedure to remove cells or tissue for examination under a microscope. Removal of the entire tissue is called excisional. Removal of a sample with an incision is called an incisional biopsy.
common_complications: Infection, bleeding, pain, or damage to the surrounding tissues.

name: Infusion (into the bloodstream)
description: A medical treatment infusing fluids or drugs into the bloodstream. Infusion therapy could occur at home, physician's office, hospital, or out-patient medical clinic.
common_complications: Superficial phlebitis caused by inflammation with or without infection at the site of the intravenous catheter. A blood clot can develop in the inflamed vein.

name: Inguinal orchiectomy (remove testicle through groin)
description: A surgical procedure to remove the testicle through an incision in the groin which may be used in the treatment of testicular cancer.
common_complications: Damage to the surrounding blood vessels and nerves. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia including allergic reactions.

name: Intramuscular injection (into a muscle)
description: A procedure to inject fluid or medication into a muscle.
common_complications: Pain, swelling or infection at the injection site.

name: Intravenous (IV, through the vein)
description: Inside a vein. Usually refers to giving fluids and/or a medication directly into a vein. The vein can be entered directly with a needle as a one-time administration or by placing a plastic catheter into the vein (intravenous line or IV).
common_complications: Superficial phlebitis caused by inflammation with or without infection at the site of the intravenous catheter. A blood clot can develop in the inflamed vein. Some medications can damage the vein and surround tissue if they leak outside the vein.

name: Intravenous pyelography IVP (x-rays of kidneys, ureters and bladder)
description: A series of x-rays to image the kidneys, ureters and bladder with a dye that is injected into the blood stream. The dye is excreted in the urine and outlines the urinary tract, including the kidneys, ureters, and bladder, with contrast material. It may help diagnose kidney stones, the cause of obstructed urine flow and certain types of kidney disease.
common_complications: The contrast dye can injure the kidneys, especially in those with pre-existing kidney disease. Patients can have allergic reactions to the dye causing a simple rash to life threatening swelling or drop in blood pressure.

name: Intubation (insert breathing tube)
description: A medical procedure to place a plastic breathing tube into the trachea (breathing tube that connects the lungs to the throat) to support ventilation and oxygenation, as well as protecting the airway by controlling any secretions.
common_complications: The teeth, mouth, throat, vocal cords or trachea can be injured while placing the tube. If patients vomit during the procedure they can breathe in stomach contents (aspiration) causing a lung infection (pneumonia).

name: Irradiation (radiation treatment)
description: A procedure using high-energy radiation to kill cancer cells. The source of the radiation may be x-rays, neutrons or gamma rays. This is also called radiation therapy.
common_complications: Injury, swelling and long-term scarring are potential risks depending on the areas being treated and the surrounding structures.

name: Joint replacement surgery
description: A surgical procedure to remove an arthritic or dysfunctional joint and replace it with an artificial joint (prosthesis). A joint is a connection between two bones. The surgery is usually done by an orthopedic surgeon and may involve a full or partial joint replacement. Most common joints to replace are hip and knee joints.
common_complications: Complications depend on which joint is being replaced. In general, they include dislocation of the new joint, loosening of hardware, breakage of hardware, and nerve or blood vessel injury during the procedure. Infection of the new joint is also a risk. Any surgery can result in pain or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus).  Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia.

name: Keratectomy (remove tissue from eye)
description: A surgical procedure done by an ophthalmologist to remove corneal tissue from the eye. Photorefractive and laser epithelial keratomileusis (LASIK) are two most common types of keratectomy and are performed to permanently improve vision.
common_complications: Serious complications are rare with poor vision being the most common complication. Infection and pain are also a risk.

name: Keratotomy (incision on the cornea)
description: A surgical procedure involving a surgical incision into the cornea of the eye. The most common reason for this procedure is cataract removal and the placement of an intra-ocular lens.
common_complications: Infection, pain, and decreased vision.

name: Laboratory test (lab work)
description: A medical procedure that tests a substance from the body, most commonly blood or urine. These tests can measure the presence or absence of chemicals, electrolytes, antibodies, or bacteria in the body. The tests are used to diagnose medical conditions, assess effectiveness of treatment, or prevent a disease. Changes of test results over time can be extremely helpful in patient monitoring.
common_complications: None.

name: Laceration repair (stitches)
description: A surgical procedure to anesthetize (usually with local anesthesia), clean, and close a wound from a traumatic injury to the soft tissues. It may involve multiple layers of closure (skin, subcutaneous, muscle, etc).
common_complications: Infection and pain. Injury to the nerves and blood vessels can occur. If the wound is not properly cleaned and a foreign body such as wood or dirt is left in the wound, a chronic infection can occur.

name: Laminectomy (remove back of vertebrae)
description: A surgical procedure to remove bony sections of the back of the spine (lamina) to relieve pressure off of a nerve. The surgery is done to relieve the narrowing of the spinal canal from spinal stenosis, degenerative disk disease, herniated disc, sciatica, and spondylosis. It is often done with a discectomy or spinal fusion.
common_complications: Nerve injury causing weakness and numbness. A collection of fluid and/or blood can require repeat surgery. The surgery can result in post-operative pain or persistent pain. May also result in infection, blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia.

name: Laminoplasty (remove pressure from spinal cord in neck)
description: A surgical procedure to cut the back of the spine (vertebra) and hinging it back to increase the size of the spinal canal. The lamina can be supported with bone struts, sutures, metal plates or spacers and tension bands. The common reason for this procedure is spinal stenosis.
common_complications: Nerve injury causing weakness and numbness. A collection of fluid and/or blood can require repeat surgery. Some patients have persistent pain. Surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus).

name: Laminotomy (make hole in back of vertebrae)
description: A surgical procedure involving a partial removal (make a hole) in the bony area at the back of the spine (vertebra) to relieve pressure of a nerve.
common_complications: Nerve injury causing weakness and numbness. A collection of fluid and/or blood can require repeat surgery. Some patients have persistent pain. Surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus).

name: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy (minimally invasive gallbladder removal)
description: A surgical procedure to remove the gallbladder. A laparoscope (camera) is inserted through a small incision, and the gallbladder is then removed through a second small incision.
common_complications: Surgery can result in pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Damage and leaking of a bile duct can result in a fluid collection and abscess (collection of pus). At times a stone can be left behind (retained stone) in one of the bile ducts. Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia.

name: Laparoscopy (camera examination inside abdomen)
description: A procedure involving the insertion of a thin, lighted tube equipped with a camera (laparoscope) through the abdominal wall to inspect the organs and tissue inside the abdomen.
common_complications: Any surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Inadvertent injury to normal surrounding structures can occur with the procedure. Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia.

name: Laparotomy  (surgically open the abdomen)
description: A surgical procedure involving an incision made in the wall of the abdomen. The procedure is done to determine an abnormality, remove damaged tissue or remove a tumor.
common_complications: The internal organs of the abdomen can be damaged. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia.

name: Laryngoscopy (camera examination inside throat)
description: A diagnostic procedure to examine the larynx (voice box) with a mirror (indirect) or with a laryngoscope (direct). Reasons for the procedure include persistent hoarseness or throat pain.
common_complications: Injury to the teeth, mouth, or throat very rarely occurs.

name: Laser (concentrated light therapy)
description: A device that concentrates light into an intense, narrow beam used to cut or destroy tissue. It is used in various procedures including microsurgery.
common_complications: Pain, swelling, and/or injury to surrounding structures. Rarely infection can occur.

name: Laser skin resurfacing (cosmetic procedure)
description: A procedure that uses a laser to remove thin layers of skin. It is preformed to treat uneven skin coloration, remove wrinkles and repair damaged skin. This procedure is also called a laser peel.
common_complications: Pain, swelling and rarely infection. Excessive scarring and uneven pigmentation can also occur.

name: Laser treatment of  spider veins
description: A procedure using a laser to treat spider veins.  Laser energy causes your spider veins to coagulate and shrink. Laser therapy is most effective for small and medium size spider veins.
common_complications: Pain, swelling and rarely infection. Excessive scarring and uneven pigmentation can rarely occur.

name: LASIK (reshape cornea)
description: A surgical procedure to reshape the cornea for improving visual acuity (ability for one to see). LASIK is the acronym for laser assisted in situ keratomileusis.
common_complications: Serious complications are rare. The most common are poor vision, dry eyes, eye irritation, scratches of the cornea, night glare and halos, and a rare form of inflammation called diffuse lamellar keratitis (DLK).

name: Lip augmentation (enlarge lips)
description: A procedure to increase the size of lips using either tissue fillers or fat. Tissue fillers, such as Radiesse and Restylane, are used to restore lost volume in the various areas of the face including the lips.
common_complications: Poor cosmetic result. Surgery can result in post-operative pain and very rarely infection.

name: Liposuction (lipoplasty, fat removal)
description: A surgical procedure to refine your figure by removing excess fat from specific areas of the body such as the abdomen, love handles, hips, buttocks, thighs, knees, arms, chin and neck.
common_complications: Poor cosmetic result, damage to nerves or blood vessels, or injury to internal organs. Surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia.

name: Lithotripsy (shock wave therapy for kidney stones)
description: A medical procedure that uses high-energy shockwaves to partially disintegrate stones inside the body such as gallstones, and urinary or kidney stones.
common_complications: Bleeding, infection, and injury to the organ involved.

name: Lobectomy (removal of part of an organ)
description: A surgical procedure involving the removal of a lobe, or portion of an organ, such as the liver, lung, breast, thyroid or brain.
common_complications: The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia.

name: Loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP, surgical tissue removal from cervix)
description: A surgical procedure involving the removal of tissue using a hot wire loop. The most common body area LEEP is used is the cervix. The procedure is done to both remove abnormal cells of the cervix and also provides a sample for microscopic analysis to diagnosis possible cancer.
common_complications: Pain, vaginal bleeding and infection.

name: Lower body lift (body recontouring)
description: A surgical procedure that involves removing the excess skin all the way around the lower abdomen, the lower back, hip and buttock region. After removing the skin, the hanging tissue of the thighs, buttock, hips and abdomen are attached to a higher location to lift the tissues back into their normal location. This tightens the skin envelope of the entire lower torso.
common_complications: Injury to nerves and blood vessels. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia.

name: Lower GI series (barium enema)
description: A diagnostic procedure using x-rays after barium is instilled into the rectum and allowed to travel backwards to fill the colon. Reasons for the procedure include lower abdominal pain, constipation and to rule out polyps or cancer.
common_complications: Occasionally constipation occurs. Rarely perforation of the rectum or colon occurs.

name: Lumbar puncture (spinal tap)
description: A medical procedure in which a needle is put into the lower part of the spinal column to collect cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), administer anesthesia, or to give anticancer drugs into the subarachnoid space.
common_complications: Infection, bleeding, and nerve injury are rare complications. The most common problem is leaking of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) causing a spinal headache (postural headache). The pain of a spinal headache decreases with lying flat and increases with standing up.

name: Lumpectomy (surgery to remove tumor from breast)
description: A surgical procedure to remove a discreet breast tumor and a small amount of normal tissue around it.
common_complications: Pain, swelling and infection. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia.

name: Lymphadenectomy (remove lymph node)
description: A procedure in which the lymph nodes are surgical removed and microscopically examined to see if they contain cancer or an infection. Also called lymph node dissection.
common_complications: Pain, infection, swelling and damage to surrounding nerves or blood vessels. After the surgery patients may experience persistent swelling of the surgical area. The surgery can result in blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Lymphangiography (diagnose lymphoma)
description: A diagnostic study of the lymphatic system involving the injection of a dye into a lymphatic vessel. The dye outlines the lymphatic vessels and organs on the x-ray. It may be helpful in making the diagnosis of lymphoma or determine the spread of other types of cancer.
