common_complications: Pain, infection or damage to the lymph channels.

name: Magnetic resonance angiography (MRA, MRI image of arteries)
description: MRI is magnetic resonance imaging, a special imaging test that does not use x-rays. MRA uses similar technology as an MRI. A chemical (usually gadolinium) is injected into the vein during the test to visualize blood vessels in the neck, brain and other parts of the body. It can be helpful in detecting abnormalities in the brain and brainstem such as aneurysm.
common_complications: Gadolinium has been associated with a serious skin and connective tissue disease called nephrogenic systemic fibrosis (NSF). People with chronic kidney disease are at increased risk of developing NSF after gadolinium. More information can be found at http://www.fda.gov/Drugs/DrugSafety/DrugSafetyNewsletter/ucm1428

name: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
description: MRI is magnetic resonance imaging, a special imaging test that does not use x-rays. A MRI uses magnetic fields to create detailed pictures inside the body and/or head. It can detect subtle changes in the tissues. A MRI is better than a CT scan (CAT scan) at identifying disease of the soft tissues such as nerves, ligaments, tendons and muscles.
common_complications: None if the contrast gadolinium is not used. Gadolinium has been associated with a serious skin and connective tissue disease called nephrogenic systemic fibrosis (NSF). Patients with chronic kidney disease are at increased risk of developing NSF after gadolinium. More information can be found at http://www.fda.gov/Drugs/DrugSafety/DrugSafetyNewsletter/ucm142889.htm.

name: Mammogram (x-ray of the breast)
description: A diagnostic procedure to x-ray the breast. Mammograms are done most often to screen for breast cancer. They are also used to help determine if a lump is more likely benign or malignant.
common_complications: Breast tissue must be compressed to get good pictures. Mammography can be uncomfortable and quite painful for some women.

name: Mastectomy (remove breast)
description: A surgical procedure to remove all or part of the breast, usually for cancer. Occasionally women choose to have a mastectomy to prevent breast cancer when there is a strong family history of breast cancer.
common_complications: The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia.

name: Mediastinoscopy (view space between lungs and heart)
description: A diagnostic procedure performed to directly view the space between the lungs and in front of the heart, including the adjacent lymph nodes. It can be helpful in making the diagnosis of lung cancer, tuberculosis, lymphoma and other conditions.
common_complications: Pain, infection and damage to surrounding tissues. The surgery can result in blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia.

name: Microwave therapy (destroy tissue with heat)
description: A procedure that destroys tissue with heat created by electrodes. The procedure may be used to damage and kill cancer cells or to make cancer cells more sensitive to the effects of radiation and/or chemotherapy.
common_complications: Pain, swelling and injury to surrounding normal tissue.

name: Myelogram (dye injected into the spinal canal)
description: A diagnostic procedure to detect abnormalities of the spine, spinal cord, or surrounding structures, involving the injection of dye during a spinal tap. The table is tilted and the dye moves to surround the spinal cord. X-rays are taken.
common_complications: Pain, bleeding at the site of the spinal tap, and injury of a nerve can occur. Infection is very rare. A headache from a spinal leak called a spinal or postural headache can also occur. Multiple exposures to radiation can increase the risk of cancer later in life.

name: Myolysis (shrink uterine growths)
description: A procedure involving the shrinking of fibroids using an electric current or a laser.
common_complications: The surgery can result in damage to nerves and blood vessels, post-operative pain, infection, vaginal bleeding or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Myomectomy (surgical removal of uterine growths)
description: Myomectomy is a procedure in which uterine fibroids are surgically removed from the uterus. The procedure is an alternative to hysterectomy (surgical removal of the uterus) in selected patients of child bearing age.
common_complications: Perforation of the uterus, injury to the intestines or pelvic blood vessels, and pelvic scarring (adhesions). The surgery can result in post-operative pain, vaginal bleeding, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Needle biopsy (remove fluid or tissue sample with a needle)
description: A procedure to remove fluid and/or cells with a needle for examination under a microscope.  Also known as a fine needle aspiration.
common_complications: Complications are uncommon, but may include infection, pain, swelling and/or injury to surrounding tissue.

name: Nephrectomy (remove kidney)
description: A surgical procedure involving the removal of a kidney that has been damaged by disease or cancer. The procedure can be performed through a laparoscope, by robot-assisted laparoscopy or with an open incision technique.
common_complications: Fluid collection and possible infection around the kidney space. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia.

name: Nerve block (block pain)
description: A procedure where a medication is injected directly into or around a nerve or into the spine to block pain.
common_complications: Injury to the nerve causing numbness or weakness.

name: Neurosurgery (surgery of the nervous system)
description: Surgical procedure involving the nervous system, such as brain and spinal surgery.
common_complications: The surgery can result in nerve injury, brain injury, post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia.

name: Nuclear medicine scan (scan with injected radioactive substances)
description: A diagnostic procedure involving small amounts of radioactive material that collects in specific areas of the body. Sophisticated instruments detect the radioactive substance in the body and process that information into an image.
common_complications: The radioactive substances are safe in most individuals.

name: Oophorectomy (remove ovaries)
description: A surgical procedure to remove one or both ovaries. An ovary is removed for large cysts, tumors, ectopic pregnancy or because of twisting (torsion) and death of the ovary. The procedure can be done through an incision (open) or through a laparoscope.
common_complications: Injury to the intestines, bladder, uterus, or pelvic blood vessels. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Open heart surgery (cardiac surgery)
description: A surgical procedure involving opening the thoracic cavity, specifically for heart valve replacements, heart bypass surgeries (coronary artery), heart transplants and other open heart procedures.
common_complications: Injury to the heart, lungs or major blood vessels of the heart and lungs. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia including allergic reactions and very rarely a heart attack or stroke.

name: Ostomy (opening in body)
description: A surgical procedure to create an opening (stoma) from an area inside the body to the outside. Colostomy, ileostomy and urostomy are types of ostomies.
common_complications: Specific complications depend on the location of the surgery. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Ovarian ablation (shut down ovaries)
description: A procedure involving surgery, radiation therapy, or a drug treatment to stop the working function of the ovaries. The procedure is typically used in the treatment of hormone receptor positive breast cancer.
common_complications: Loss of normal hormonal function causing early menopause symptoms.

name: Palliative therapy (care given to improve quality of life)
description: A medical treatment given to relieve symptoms caused by advanced disease. Palliative therapy does not alter the course of a disease, but can improve the quality of life for suffering patients.
common_complications: None.

name: Pancreaticoduodenectomy (remove pancreas and duodenum)
description: A surgical procedure for pancreatic cancer involving removal of the pancreas and part of the duodenum. It is also known as the Whipple procedure.
common_complications: Poor absorption of nutrients and diabetes after the procedure. Injury to the intestines, blood vessels or other internal organs of the abdomen. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia.

name: Pap test (screening exam for cervical cancer)
description: A diagnostic procedure to collect cells from the cervix for examination under a microscope. It is helpful in diagnosing cancer or cellular changes that may lead to cancer, and can show noncancerous conditions, such as infection or inflammation. May also be referred to as a Pap smear.
common_complications: None.

name: Patient controlled anesthesia (PCA pump, self-administered pain pump)
description: A medical treatment giving the patient control over the amount of pain medicine that is used. When pain relief is needed, the person can receive a preset dose of pain medicine by pressing a button on a computerized pump that is connected to an IV. A PCA pumped is often used with patients having severe pain or immediately after surgery.
common_complications: Overdose of medication causing depressed respiratory effort and rarely death.

name: Pelvic laparoscopy (camera examination inside lower abdomen)
description: A surgical procedure to examine and treat abdominal and pelvic organs involving a laparoscope which is inserted into the abdomen. It is helpful in detecting pelvic inflammatory disease, endometriosis, ovarian cysts, and other conditions.
common_complications: Injury to the intestines, bladder, ureter (tube connecting kidney to the bladder), or pelvic blood vessels. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Percutaneous transhepatic cholangiography (PTC, x-ray of the bile ducts)
description: A diagnostic procedure to image the hepatic and common bile ducts. Contrast is injected through the skin into the liver or bile duct, and the ducts are then x-rayed to find the point of obstruction. It may be helpful in making the diagnosis of gallstones, liver cancer and other conditions. Since there are less invasive ways to image the biliary tree (MRI or CT scan), the procedure is usually only done to drain a blocked a biliary system.
common_complications: Infection and/or pain. Damage to the liver, intestine, liver blood vessels or bile ducts.

name: Percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA, minimally invasive therapy to open up blocked heart arteries)
description: A procedure to open clogged or blocked arteries in the heart. A catheter with a tiny balloon at its tip is inserted into an artery in the groin or arm. The catheter is advanced into the narrowed coronary artery, with a tiny balloon at its tip. The balloon is then inflated and deflated sequentially to break open the narrowing and allow more passage of blood. A wire mesh stent is often left inside the vessel to keep it open.
common_complications: Infection, pain and swelling at the site of catheter insertion. Damage to the blood vessels of the heart, leg, or arm rarely requiring immediate surgery. The contrast used can injure the kidneys, especially if the person has underlying kidney disease. Some patients can be allergic to the contrast causing a reaction from a rash to life threatening swelling or drop in blood pressure.

name: PET CT scan (positron emission tomography and computed tomography)
description: A diagnostic procedure combining CT (computed tomography) and PET (positron emission tomography). This can provide a more complete picture of a tumor's location and growth or spread than either test done independently. It can also be used to help find the site of infection.
common_complications: Rarely allergic reactions can occur.

name: Plasmapheresis (replacement of the liquid in blood)
description: The procedure consists of removal of blood, separation of blood cells from plasma, and return of the blood cells to the body's circulation. The blood cells are typically diluted with a saline solution and a blood protein called albumin. Plasmapheresis is done to treat diseases such as TTP (thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura) and Guillain-Barre.
common_complications: Infection of the blood from the insertion of the catheter. Allergic reactions ranging from a rash to life threatening swelling and low blood pressure can occur.

name: Photodynamic therapy (PDT, cancer therapy using light)
description: A treatment used to kill cancer cells or other abnormal cells by first administering  a photo-active medication followed by special light therapy.
common_complications: Sunburn like skin and allergic reactions.

name: Photorefractive keratectomy (remove surface layer of cornea)
description: A procedure to remove the surface layer of the cornea by gentle scraping and use of a computer-controlled excimer laser to reshape the stroma. The procedure is generally done to improve vision.
common_complications: Infection, pain, and decreased vision.

name: Pneumonectomy (remove lung)
description: A surgical procedure to remove an entire lung. It is usually done to treat lung cancer.
common_complications: Injury to the heart, blood vessels of the heart or lungs, or other organs in the chest. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia including allergic reactions and very rarely a heart attack or stroke.

name: Port (medical appliance installed beneath skin)
description: A surgically implanted device for drawing blood and infusing medications into the blood stream without repeated needle sticks into veins. Also called a Port-A-Cath.
common_complications: Infection, pain and/or the formation of a blood clot in the vein.

name: Positron emission tomography scan (PET scan)
description: A diagnostic procedure involving a computerized image of the metabolic activity of body tissues used to determine the presence of disease, most often cancer or infection.
common_complications: Rarely an allergic reaction can occur.

name: Proctosigmoidoscopy (lower colon diagnostic test)
description: A procedure to image the lower colon with a thin, lighted tube called a sigmoidoscope. Reasons for the procedure include screening for colorectal cancer and to help diagnose infections and inflammatory bowel disease, such as Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis. Also known as a sigmoidoscopy.
common_complications: Pain and bloating. Injury to the rectum or lower colon. Colonic perforation can rarely occur.

name: Prostatectomy (remove prostate)
description: A surgical procedure to remove part or the entire prostate. Radical (or total) prostatectomy is the removal of the entire prostate and some of the tissue around it.
common_complications: Impotence and problems urinating.  Injury to the bladder, intestines, or pelvic blood vessels. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia including allergic reactions and very rarely a heart attack or stroke.

name: Proton magnetic resonance spectroscopic imaging (imaging test that measures cell activity)
description: A diagnostic procedure to detect and measure activity at the cellular level. It provides chemical information and is used in conjunction with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), which gives anatomical information. It can also be called 1H-nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopic imaging.
common_complications: Complications are rare.

name: Radial keratotomy (RK, correct nearsightedness)
description: A surgical procedure to correct myopia (nearsightedness) by flattening the cornea.
common_complications: Infection, pain and decreased vision.

name: Radiation surgery (radiosurgery)
description: A procedure involving radiation therapy delivered to a tumor while sparing the healthy tissue. Also called radiosurgery and stereotactic external beam irradiation. It is used most frequently in the treatment of brain tumors.
common_complications: Injury to surrounding normal brain causing weakness, numbness, and loss of other brain function.

name: Radiation therapy (radiotherapy)
description: A procedure using high-energy radiation to kill cancer cells. The source of the radiation may be x-rays, neutrons or gamma rays.
common_complications: Damage to normal surrounding tissues.

name: Radical cystectomy (complete bladder removal)
description: A surgical procedure to remove the bladder as well as nearby tissues and affected organs for the treatment of bladder cancer.
common_complications: Injury to the intestines or pelvic blood vessels. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia including allergic reactions and very rarely a heart attack or stroke.

name: Radical lymph node dissection (surgical removal of lymph nodes and surrounding tissue)
description: A surgical procedure in which the lymph nodes are removed and examined to see whether they contain cancer. Also called lymph node dissection or lymphadenectomy.
common_complications: Injury to nerves and surrounding blood vessels. The arm or leg being served by the lymph nodes can have chronic swelling called lymphedema. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia.

name: Radical mastectomy (remove breast, chest muscles and lymph nodes)
description: A surgical procedure in which the breast, chest muscles, and all of the lymph nodes under the arm are removed, usually for breast cancer.
common_complications: Fluid collections (seroma), injury to blood vessels or nerves. Chronic swelling may occur in the upper extremity that the lymph nodes were removed. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia.

name: Radical prostatectomy (surgical removal of prostate and surrounding tissue)
description: A surgical procedure to remove the entire prostate and some of the tissue around it.
common_complications: Impotence and problems urinating. Injury to the bladder, intestines, or pelvic blood vessels. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia including allergic reactions and very rarely a heart attack or stroke.

name: Radiofrequency ablation (destroy tissue with heat)
description: A procedure involving electrodes used to heat and destroy abnormal tissue. It is used in the treatment of a variety of conditions including certain types of arrhythmias and cancers.
common_complications: Injury to surrounding normal tissue and structures.

name: Radionuclide scanning (body part imaging with small amounts of radioactive material)
description: A diagnostic procedure where a patient swallows or is injected with a small amount of radioactive material and then a machine measures the radioactivity in certain organs.
common_complications: Complications are rare.

name: Reconstructive surgery (reshape body part)
description: A surgical procedure to reshape or reconstruct a part of the body changed by a previous surgery, accident or disease.
common_complications: Injury to blood vessels or nerves. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Refractive surgery (vision correction surgery)
description: A surgical procedure to improve vision by correcting refractive errors, such as nearsightedness, farsightedness, or astigmatism.
common_complications: Infection, pain, or decreased vision.

name: Resection (remove tissue)
description: A surgical procedure to remove tissue, organ or structure from the body. A resection could entail a partial or complete removal of a structure or organ.
common_complications: The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Rhinoplasty (nose job)
description: A surgical procedure to reduce excess cartilage and bone in the nose for cosmetic reasons, providing a straighter and/or smaller appearance. The procedure can also help to correct breathing problems associated with the nose.
common_complications: Poor cosmetic result. The surgery can result in post-operative pain and/or infection. Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Robotic surgery (robot assisted surgery)
description: A surgical procedure assisted by robotic arms that perform the surgery with a variety of surgical tools. The robotic arms give surgeons more intricate motion and tool control for complex surgeries. It is used for a variety of surgeries within surgical subspecialties such as gynecology, urology, general surgery, and cardiothoracic surgery.
common_complications: Injury to normal surrounding structures. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Salpingectomy (remove fallopian tubes)
description: A surgical procedure to remove one or both fallopian tubes. The most common reasons for removal are tumors, ectopic pregnancy or in association with removal of the ovaries.
common_complications: Injury to the bladder, intestines or pelvic blood vessels. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Salpingo oophorectomy (remove fallopian tubes and ovaries)
description: A surgical procedure to remove the fallopian tubes and ovaries. Reasons why this surgery may be needed include cysts, tumors, ectopic pregnancy, or after twisting of the ovary (torsion).
common_complications: Injury to the bladder, intestines or pelvic blood vessels. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Sclerotherapy (collapse varicose veins)
description: A procedure to remove spider veins and varicose veins. A chemical called a sclerosing solution is injected into the veins causing them to collapse and contract. The procedure is best suited for medium sized spider veins and larger since a needle must be inserted into the vein. It may require multiple treatments for the desired effect.
common_complications: Scarring, bleeding, infection, skin numbness, damage to deeper structures, skin bumps, skin puckering, skin discoloration, skin ulceration and pain.

name: Sigmoidoscopy (camera examination of the lower colon)
description: A procedure to image the lower colon with a thin, lighted tube called a sigmoidoscope. Reasons for the procedure include screening for colorectal cancer and to help diagnose infections and inflammatory bowel disease, such as Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis.
common_complications: Pain and abdominal boating. Injury to the rectum or lower colon. Colonic perforation can rarely occur.

name: Sonogram (imaging test using sound waves)
description: A diagnostic imaging procedure. The ultrasound device makes sound waves that bounce off tissues and create echoes. Its used routinely during pregnancy to image the fetus. The pictures can be used to diagnose abnormalities of vascular structures, liver, gallbladder, spleen, appendix, pancreas, kidneys, thyroid, heart and other conditions. Also known as an ultrasound test.
common_complications: None.

name: Spinal fusion (fusing vertebra)
description: A spinal fusion is the locking together (fusing) of multiple spinal vertebrae of the back to help relieve the pressure placed on the nerves from movement of the spine. It may also include removing the disc between two vertebrae and inserting bone graft into the space created between the two vertebral bodies. The bone graft can be taken from the patient's hip (autograft bone) during the spine fusion surgery, harvested from cadaver bone (allograft bone) or manufactured (synthetic bone graft substitute). The surgery may be done to relieve the pain and numbness caused by herniated disc, spinal stenosis, or spondylolisthesis.
common_complications: Complications include: vertebrae failing to fuse, hardware fracture, bone graft migration, nerve damage or persistent pain. All surgery comes with the risk of infection and blood clots. Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia.

name: Splenectomy (remove spleen)
description: A surgical procedure to remove the spleen. The major reasons for splenectomy are trauma, spontaneous rupture, cancer, low platelets (thrombocytopenia), and other blood diseases.
common_complications: Without a spleen, there is an increased risk of certain bacterial infections. The surgery can result in damage to the intestines or adjacent blood vessels. Post-operative pain, blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Stent (mesh tube to treat narrow or weak blood vessels)
description: A medical device placed inside a blood vessel to hold it open after it is expanded. It is commonly used for keeping coronary arteries open after angioplasty. Some of the coronary stents contain medications to help prevent the vessel from closing again (drug eluding stent). Stents are also used to hold open other narrowed structures, such as a ureters, bile ducts and pancreatic ducts.
common_complications: The artery with the stent can become blocked with the formation of a new blood clot or scar tissue. Rarely placement of a coronary stent can tear the artery requiring emergent surgery to bypass the vessel.

name: Stereotactic biopsy (removal of tissue aided by computer and scanner)
description: A diagnostic procedure using computer and scanning technologies to find a tumor site and guide the removal of tissue for examination under a microscope. It can be helpful in obtaining a biopsy in complex presentations of breast cancer, brain tumors, and other types of cancer.
common_complications: Infection, pain or injury to surrounding normal tissue.

name: Stereotactic radiosurgery (brain tumor treatment)
description: A medical procedure involving a rigid head frame that is attached to the skull for the accurate administration of radiation therapy through openings in the head frame. The radiation is more accurately aimed using detailed CT scan and MRI imaging. This allows for treatment of a tumor while decreasing  radiation exposure to normal brain tissue.
common_complications: Injury to surrounding normal brain causing weakness, numbness, and loss of other brain function.

name: Stress test (test for heart disease)
description: A medical diagnostic procedure used to record electrical activity of the heart during exercise. This helps a doctor determine how well your heart can handle exercise. This test is commonly used to help diagnose coronary artery disease, predict risk for a heart attack, or to monitor known heart conditions.  Also known as an exercise stress test.
common_complications: Rarely a patient can have a heart attack or abnormal beating of the heart (arrhythmia) during the procedure.

name: Surgery (invasive treatment or diagnostic procedure)
description: A procedure that cuts into tissue to diagnose, treat, remove, and/or repair the body.
common_complications: Potential complications are almost none to some that are very serious, including death. For example, major surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients that need general anesthesia have infrequent allergic reactions and very rarely a heart attack or stroke.

name: Swan Ganz catheter placement (tube in jugular vein to measure heart pressures)
description: A procedure to thread a special intravenous catheter through the skin and into the internal jugular vein. The catheter is advanced into the heart to obtain accurate readings of pulmonary artery pressure and left atrial pressure.
common_complications: Infection and pain at the insertion site. Injury to the blood vessel and/or blood clot in the vessel. Insertion of the catheter can cause a collapsed lung (pneumothorax) or bleeding in the lung.

name: Thallium stress test (chemical test for heart disease)
description: A diagnostic procedure used to take pictures of the heart during exercise. A small amount of radioactive material is injected into a vein and is used to visualize blood flow to the heart muscle. This helps a doctor determine cardiac blood flow during exercise. This test is commonly used to help diagnose coronary artery disease, predict risk for a heart attack, or to monitor a known heart condition.
common_complications: Rarely patients can have a heart attack or a life threatening abnormal beating of the heart (arrhythmia) during the exercise.

name: Thermal ablation (heat to remove tissue)
description: A surgical procedure using heat to remove or destroy tissue.
common_complications: Damage to adjacent normal structures and tissue.

name: Thigh lift (remove skin and fat from thighs)
description: A surgical procedure involving removal of the excess skin and fat of the thighs that can occur with aging, weight loss, and loss of skin elasticity. It can improve the appearance of loose, saggy thighs and is often done in conjunction with other procedures, such as, tummy tuck or arm lifts, in patients who have significant weight loss after gastric bypass surgery.
common_complications: Injury to blood vessels and nerves, and a poor cosmetic result. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Thoracoscopy (camera examination inside chest)
description: A surgical procedure using an endoscope to examine the inside of the chest. Reasons for the procedure include needing a direct view of the lung and the lining surround the lung and taking biopsies to rule out cancer and other conditions.
common_complications: Injury to blood vessels, and lungs. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Thoracotomy (invasive surgery to examine inside the chest)
description: A surgical procedure to open the chest which is useful in the diagnosis and/or treatment of lung cancer, heart disease, and other conditions.
common_complications: Injury to the heart and lungs. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia including allergic reactions and very rarely a heart attack or stroke.

name: Thyroidectomy (remove thyroid)
description: A surgical procedure to remove part or the entire thyroid gland. The thyroid gland is removed because of a worrisome nodule, cancer, an overactive thyroid gland (hyperthyroidism), or non-cancerous thyroid growth or inflammation (goiter).
common_complications: Injury to the parathyroid gland causing low calcium levels. Nerve injury resulting in hoarseness. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia.

name: Tilt table test (evaluates fainting spells)
description: A diagnostic test to evaluate unexplained positional fainting spells or syncope.  Heart rate, blood pressure and other measurements are recorded while the patient is tilted at different angles. The test is usually performed to help diagnose vasodepressor syncope.
common_complications: Feeling lightheaded, transient nausea, sweating, weakness. Vomiting may occur.

name: Total hip replacement
description: A surgical procedure to replace the hip with an artificial joint. The cup shaped hip socket and the ball of the thigh bone are replaced with metal and plastic components.  The most common reasons for hip replacement are arthritis and other conditions that cause significant damage to the cartilage and bone of the joint.
common_complications: Joint dislocation, bone fracture, hardware fracture, loosening of the joint, and change in leg length are all risks. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia including allergic reactions and very rarely a heart attack or stroke.

name: Total knee replacement
description: A surgical procedure to replace the knee with an artificial joint. The damaged cartilage and bone of the knee joint are replaced with a combination of metal and plastic components. The most common reason for knee replacement is arthritis or other conditions which cause significant damage to the cartilage and bone of the joint.
common_complications: Knee stiffness, blood loss and nerve injury are risks. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia including allergic reactions and very rarely a heart attack or stroke.

name: Tracheostomy (tracheotomy, opening in windpipe)
description: A surgical procedure to establish an opening (stoma) into the windpipe (trachea). It may be needed after part of the windpipe is removed for cancer, because of traumatic injury or if the person has severe lung damage requiring prolonged use of a breathing tube.
common_complications: Scarring of the trachea (stenosis), infection, and damage to the blood vessels of the neck. Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Transabdominal ultrasound (ultrasound image of abdomen)
description: A diagnostic imaging procedure. The ultrasound device is pressed against the abdomen, and sound waves from the device bounce off tissues and create echoes. The pictures can be used to diagnose abnormalities of the liver, gallbladder, spleen, appendix, pancreas, kidneys and aorta (for example, an aortic aneurysm). Also known as abdominal ultrasound.
common_complications: None.

name: Transcutaneous electric nerve stimulation (TENS, pain management)
description: A medical device sometimes helpful for treating chronic pain. A small power pack connected to two electrodes delivers mild electric currents to specific areas of the skin.
common_complications: Usually none, but some patients get little or no pain relief from the device).

name: Transfusion (blood replacement through a vein)
description: A medical treatment providing blood components or whole blood into the bloodstream. It may involve the person's stored blood, or blood donated for this use. Transfusions most often occur for low blood count from bleeding or anemia.
common_complications: Even after cross matching of blood reactions can occur. Severe reactions cause fever, shortness of breath, chest pain and rarely shock. Milder reactions include hives, itching and a feeling of uneasiness. Infection is another rare complication.

name: Transplantation (replace organ)
description: A surgical procedure to replace an organ with one from another person.
common_complications: The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia. The medications used to prevent organ rejection depress the immune system leading to increased risk of infection. Some of these infections can be life threatening.

name: Transrectal ultrasound (ultrasound image through rectum)
description: A diagnostic imaging procedure. An ultrasound (sonogram) consists of high frequency sound waves. An ultrasound transducer is inserted into the rectum to view the prostate.
common_complications: Rarely minor injury to the rectum can occur.

name: Transurethral resection (TURP, removal of part or all of prostate)
description: A surgical procedure performed with a special instrument inserted through the urethra. It is done most often to treat an enlarged prostate.
common_complications: Impotence, inability to urinate, semen entering the bladder (retrograde ejaculation), and bloody urine. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia including allergic reactions and very rarely a heart attack or stroke.

name: Transvaginal ultrasound (ultrasound image through vagina)
description: A diagnostic procedure used to examine the uterus, fallopian tubes, ovaries and bladder using sound waves to create images. An ultrasound probe is inserted into the vagina to get the most detailed pictures.
common_complications: None.

name: Tummy tuck (abdominoplasty)
description: A surgical procedure involving an incision in the bikini area, just above the pubic hair line. The skin and fat of the abdomen is then lifted off of the muscle layer. If needed, the muscle layer is tightened with a row of stitches above and below the belly button. Meanwhile, the belly button is left attached to the muscle layer. The excess skin and fat is then pulled and stretched down to the incision and removed. A small opening is then created in order to relocate the belly button.
common_complications: Collection of fluid in the abdominal wall and infection. The surgery can result in post-operative pain or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia. The procedure might not result in the desired cosmetic outcome.

name: Ultrasound test (imaging test using sound waves)
description: A diagnostic imaging procedure. The ultrasound device makes sound waves that bounce off tissues and create echoes. Its used routinely during pregnancy to image the fetus. The pictures can be used to diagnose abnormalities of vascular structures, liver, gallbladder, spleen, appendix, pancreas, kidneys, thyroid, heart and other organs. Also known as a sonogram.
common_complications: None.

name: Upper arm lift (remove skin and fat from arm)
description: A surgical procedure involving removal of unwanted skin and fat from the inner side of the upper arm.
common_complications: The surgery can result in post-operative pain, poor cosmetic results, and/or infection. Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Upper GI series (x-ray image of upper digestive tract)
description: A diagnostic procedure to x-ray the esophagus, stomach and small intestine. The x-rays are taken after the person drinks a barium solution, which coats the inner lining of the upper digestive organs.
common_complications: Complications are very rare. A person with swallowing difficulties might have barium enter the airway causing aspiration pneumonia.

name: Urostomy (artificial opening for the urinary system)
description: A surgical procedure creating an opening from the urinary tract to the outside of the body, for the excretion of urine. It is usually done to relieve obstruction of urinary flow.
common_complications: The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Uterine ablation (remove uterus lining)
description: A surgical procedure that scars the lining of the uterus. A common indication is for excessive menstrual bleeding. The procedure can sometimes prevent a hysterectomy.
common_complications: Pain, infection, vaginal bleeding, damage to the cervix, and perforation of the uterus.

name: Uterine fibroid embolization (cut blood supply to uterine growths)
description: A procedure to cut off the blood supply for uterine fibroids to shrink them. It is also called uterine artery embolization.
common_complications: Pain. Diminished blood supply to the ovaries, which could result in infertility. Extensive damage to the uterus because of decreased blood supply, which might require hysterectomy. Infection and blood clots can also occur.

name: Vaginal hysterectomy (removal of the uterus through the vagina)
description: A surgical procedure to remove the uterus through the vagina. It avoids needing to make an abdominal incision and scar.
common_complications: Injury to the bladder or pelvic vessels. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Voiding cystourethrogram (x-ray of bladder function)
description: A procedure that uses x-rays to evaluate the bladder and lower urinary tract. A small tube (catheter) is inserted through the urethra and into the bladder and the bladder is filled with contrast dye. X-rays are taken while the patient empties their bladder. This test can be used to diagnose injuries and diseases of the bladder and urethra.
common_complications: Rarely injury to the urethra and urinary infection.

name: Xeroradiography (x-ray on paper)
description: A diagnostic procedure where a picture of the body is recorded on paper rather than on film.
common_complications: Complications are rare.

name: X-ray (image bones and soft tissue)
description: A diagnostic test to image parts of the body, including some soft tissues and bones. In high doses, x-rays are used to treat cancer.
common_complications: Multiple exposures to radiation increase the risk of cancer later in life.

name: Bariatric surgery (weight loss surgery)
description: Bariatric surgery, also called weight loss surgery, is a general description of surgery that helps obese people lose weight. The two most common procedures performed are gastric bypass surgery and gastric banding. These procedures result in significant long-term weight loss, better blood sugar control in people with type 2 diabetes, and improvement in cardiovascular risk factors.
common_complications: Bariatric surgery can result in an intra-abdominal infection, intestinal obstruction, or damage to other organs in the abdomen. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, wound infection and/or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to the general anesthesia including allergic reactions and very rarely a heart attack or stroke. Some patients experience persistent frequent vomiting, low blood sugar, and nutritional deficiencies (B12 and vitamin D are the most common).

name: Gastric banding (stomach stapling)
description: Gastric banding is one of the most common types of bariatric surgery, a surgical procedure performed to help obese people lose weight. The surgery is often done through a laparoscope. An adjustable band is placed around the stomach, which decreases the amount of food a person can consume. Sutures or staples can be used instead of the band to make the stomach smaller. Gastric banding usually results in significant long-term weight loss, better blood sugar control in people with type 2 diabetes, and improvement in cardiovascular risk factors.
common_complications: After the surgery, infection and blood clots in the legs and lung are always a possibility. Other complications include frequent vomiting, low blood sugar, and nutritional deficiencies. Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Tooth extraction (remove tooth)
description: Tooth extraction is the removal of a tooth from its socket in the bone. A tooth may need to be extracted if it is too damaged to be repaired with a filling, crown, or other treatment. A very loose tooth may also require extraction if too much bone has been lost. Wisdom teeth, also called third molars, are often extracted. Sometimes they get stuck in the jaw (impacted) and do not come in. If pain and swelling occur, they need to be extracted. Most simple extractions can be done using just a local anesthetic. Surgical extractions may also use anesthesia through a vein (intravenous). Some people may need general anesthesia.
common_complications: Discomfort, swelling, and some bleeding are common after tooth extraction. The level of pain and how long it lasts will depend on how difficult it was to remove the tooth. Dry socket develops in about 3% to 4% of all extractions. This occurs when a blood clot doesn't form in the hole or the blood clot breaks off or breaks down too early. Infection is possible but unlikely. Other risks include accidental damage to nearby teeth, an incomplete extraction, fractured jaw, hole in the sinus, soreness in the jaw muscle or joint, or numbness.

name: Myectomy surgery (removal of muscle)
description: Surgical procedure to remove a small amount of muscle from an organ.  For example, surgery can be performed on the heart to remove thickened muscle blocking blood flow or the uterus to remove fibroids. Surgical method may vary depending on the location of the procedure on the body.
common_complications: The surgery can result in damage to nerves and blood vessels, post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Gamma knife radiosurgery (noninvasive brain surgery)
description: A type of stereotactic radiosurgery used to treat brain tumors. The medical procedure involves a rigid head frame that is attached to the skull for the accurate administration of radiation therapy through openings in the head frame. The radiation is more accurately aimed using detailed CT scan and MRI imaging. This allows for treatment of a tumor while decreasing the amount of radiation given to normal brain tissue. Gamma knife surgery is also used to treat abnormal blood vessel formations (AVMs) and trigeminal neuralgia.
common_complications: Injury to surrounding normal tissue. When used for brain tumors, it may result in weakness, numbness, and loss of other brain function.

name: Exercise stress test (heart test during exercise)
description: A medical diagnostic procedure used to record electrical activity of the heart during exercise. This helps a doctor determine how well your heart can handle exercise. This test is commonly used to help diagnose coronary artery disease, predict risk for a heart attack, or to monitor known heart condition.  Also known as a stress test.
common_complications: Rarely a patient can have a heart attack or abnormal beating of the heart (arrhythmia) during the procedure.

name: Kyphoplasty (spinal fracture treatment)
description: A surgical procedure for compression fractures of the spine (vertebra). A small incision is made in the back. Using x-ray guidance, a needle is inserted at the level of the compression fracture in the spine.  A balloon is first inflated in the fracture to restore height. A cement-like substance that solidifies is then injected into a fractured vertebra to stabilize it.
common_complications: Pain and infection at the skin puncture site. Accidental injection of cement into the spinal canal can cause nerve damage and paralysis on rare occasions. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR)
description: CPR can be a life-saving technique. It helps maintain circulation with or without breathing until emergency medical help arrives. CPR can be used on people who have had a heart attack, drowned or other serious illness where there is no heart beat or breathing. Here is what the American Heart Association recommends for untrained people at http://handsonlycpr.org/. It's not normal to see an adult suddenly collapse but if you do call 911 and push hard and fast in the center of the chest. Don't be afraid. Your actions can only help. Take a minute and look around this site and invite your friends! Increasing the number of people who know about Hands-Only TM CPR will increase the chance to save a life.
common_complications: While broken ribs and vomiting can be complications of CPR, the American Heart Association believes not taking action with someone who has just collapsed is more harmful than the potential complications.

name: Urine Cortisol 24 hour collection (urine test to measure hormone from adrenal gland)
description: A urine test that measures the amount of the steroid hormone cortisol excreted into the urine over a 24-hour period. The test is typically done to diagnose over active adrenal glands (Cushing's  disease).
common_complications: None.

name: Arterial blood gas (ABG, analysis of arterial blood)
description: The test measures the acidity (pH) and the levels of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the blood. A needle is inserted into an artery to obtain a small amount of blood. An ABG measures how well the lungs are functioning and is useful in asthma, COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) and other lung conditions. It is also helpful in disorders that affect the acidity level of blood, such as diabetic ketoacidosis.
common_complications: Pain and swelling at the needle insertion site. Rarely there can be damage to the artery with bleeding.

name: Acetaminophen (Tylenol) level
description: Acetaminophen is the generic name for Tylenol. A blood level is measured to determine if too much has been taken. This is important since there is an antidote. If left untreated acetaminophen poisoning can lead to liver toxicity and death.
common_complications: None

name: Activated partial thromboplastin (PTT)
description: Partial thromboplastin time (PTT) is a blood test that measures the blood's ability to clot. A common medication called heparin increases the PTT and the doctor measures the value to know how much heparin should be given.
common_complications: None

name: Air contrast enema (x-ray study of the colon)
description: A diagnostic procedure in which a barium-containing solution and air are put into the rectum and colon from the anus. Barium coats the lining of the rectum and large intestine. The air helps keep the colon distended as X-rays are taken. This procedure can help diagnose colorectal cancer, ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease, and other diseases of the colon.
common_complications: Damage to the rectum or colon can rarely occur.

name: Allergy testing
description: Allergy testing is done to determine if a patient is allergic to a substance. There are three basic types of allergy testing: skin testing, elimination test, and a blood test. With a skin test a substance is put in contact with the skin and the reaction of the skin is measured. Elimination testing is performed by removing foods from the diet and observing symptoms. Blood testing is done to measure the presence of antibodies and eosinophils after the exposure to a potential allergen.
common_complications: Rarely the allergic reaction being induced with skin testing can be severe and life threatening.

name: Antinuclear antibody (ANA, blood test for autoimmune disease)
description: An antinuclear antibody test is done help diagnose autoimmune diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). However, a positive test does not always mean the person has an autoimmune disease. Many health people, especially women, have a positive ANA.
common_complications: None.

name: Analysis of joint fluid (synovial fluid)
description: A needle is inserted into a joint and fluid is removed. The fluid from the joint (synovial fluid) is analyzed for blood cells, bacteria, proteins and crystals. The test is used to diagnose joint infections, gout, certain types of arthritis, and traumatic injuries.
common_complications: Pain and swelling at the test site. Infection can be introduced into the skin or the joint. Injury to a tendon, nerve or blood vessel can rarely occur.

name: Androgen (male sex hormone)
description: A male sex hormone that is measured to typically detect a deficiency.
common_complications: None

name: Anoscopy (tube to view the anus, rectum)
description: Anoscopy is performed by inserting a tube into the rectum to look at the lining of the rectum. The test is done to determine the cause of rectal bleeding or pain, most often related to hemorrhoids or inflammation.
common_complications: Rarely the rectum can be injured.

name: Antibody (immune system blood test)
description: An antibody is a type of protein the body makes to attack foreign substances that enter the body, such as a bacteria or viruses. Antibodies are also made against chemicals, pollen and other allergic substances. Sometimes the immune system makes antibodies against normal tissues (autoantibodies). The presence and level of antibodies in blood can also be used to help diagnose specific diseases.
common_complications: None

name: Aortography (x-ray of aorta)
description: The aorta is the large artery that arises from the heart and supplies blood to the entire body. Aortography is an examination of the aorta using x-rays after the injection of contrast dye.
common_complications: Injury to the artery during injection of the contrast dye. The contrast can injure the kidneys, especially if the person has underlying kidney disease. Some patients can have an allergic reaction to the dye. The allergic reaction can be mild to severe.

name: Arthrocentesis (joint fluid removal)
description: A procedure to remove joint fluid by inserting a needle into a joint. The fluid is then tested to help diagnose infections, arthritis, gout or traumatic injuries. The procedure is sometimes done to remove the buildup of fluid in the joint, giving pain relief to the patient. Sometimes the doctor will insert medication at the same time.
common_complications: Pain and swelling at the needle insertion test site. Rarely infection of the skin or the joint. Injury to a tendon, nerve or blood vessel can rarely occur.

name: Aspirin (salicylate) level
description: A blood test to measure the amount of aspirin in the blood. Too high an aspirin level either accidentally or intentionally can be life threatening.
common_complications: None

name: B12 test (blood test for vitamin)
description: B12 is a vitamin and the level can be measured in the blood. Low levels can cause anemia and malfunctioning of the nerves.
common_complications: None

name: Beta human chorionic gonadotropin (BHCG, pregnancy hormone)
description: BHCG (Beta human chorionic gonadotropin) is produced during pregnancy and is measured in the urine or blood to diagnose a pregnancy. In pregnancy the hormone is made by the placenta and can be detected as early as 11 days after becoming pregnant. The hormone is also elevated in certain tumors.
common_complications: None

name: Bladder biopsy (bladder sample)
description: A bladder biopsy is a procedure that involves taking a piece of the lining of the bladder for examination. The doctor uses a scope that is inserted through the urethra into the bladder (cystoscopy) to obtain the sample.
common_complications: Injury to the urethra and bladder. Urinary tract infection.

name: Bleeding time (clotting blood test)
description: Bleeding time is a test to measure how long it takes for the blood to clot. A prolonged bleeding time can occur because of low levels of clotting proteins and/or inadequate platelet activity.
common_complications: None

name: Blood alcohol level (ethanol level)
description: The blood alcohol level (ethanol level) measures the amount of alcohol in the blood. The clinical effects of a particular alcohol level can vary greatly between different people depending on how often they drink alcohol and their body size.
common_complications: None

name: Blood culture (test for infection in blood)
description: A blood culture is a laboratory test to check for bacteria or other micro-organisms in the blood. This test is done when the doctor suspects a serious infection.
common_complications: None

name: Blood smear (microscopic blood evaluation)
description: A blood smear is a blood test that is used to evaluate the number and shape of the blood cells. The test is done to help diagnose blood disorders, such as anemia and leukemia.
common_complications: None

name: Botulism toxin assay (blood test to diagnose botulism)
description: A test to detect the toxin of Clostridium botulinum, the bacterial toxin that causes botulism. The test can be done on blood, stool, vomit, or stomach contents.
common_complications: None

name: Blood type
description: A blood test to identify a person's red blood cell type. A blood type is done prior to a blood transfusion to determine which type of blood to give a patient.
common_complications: None

name: Brain natriuretic peptide (BNP, blood test for heart failure)
description: A brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) test is a blood test done to help diagnose heart failure.
common_complications: None

name: Caloric stimulation (test of ear and brain connection)
description: Caloric stimulation is a test which checks the connection between the balance system of the ear, the acoustic nerve and the part of the brain that controls balance. Warm or cold water placed in the ear causes specific rapid eye movements that help determine normal function.
common_complications: Dizziness, nausea and vomiting

name: Carboxyhemoglobin level (carbon monoxide blood test)
description: The carboxyhemoglobin level is a measure of the amount of carbon monoxide in the blood. Carbon monoxide poisoning is a life threatening disease. Early diagnosis and removal from the toxic environment improves outcome.
common_complications: None

name: Cardiac event monitor (recording of heart's electrical activity)
description: A cardiac event monitor is a heart monitor that a patient wears to detect difficult to diagnose heart rhythm abnormalities. The patient wears the monitor for up to 30 days. When symptoms such as lightheadedness or palpitations occur, the patient pushes a button to record an ECG strip. The recording can often be transmitted by phone to the monitor company.
common_complications: None

name: Cervical culture (test for infection in female organ)
description: During a pelvic exam the healthcare provider takes a sample from the cervix of the uterus using a swab. The sample is sent to the laboratory for bacterial culture. Most often this includes testing for gonorrhea and chlamydia.
common_complications: None

name: Chem-12 (comprehensive metabolic panel, blood test)
description: A Chem-12 is also called a Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP) or a SMA-12. This test measures blood chemistries and proteins that help diagnose many conditions including diabetes, kidney and liver diseases. The Chem-12 tests for electrolytes (sodium, potassium, carbon dioxide, and chloride), kidney tests (creatinine, blood urea nitrogen), proteins (albumin, total protein), liver tests (alkaline phosphatase, alanine amino transferase, aspartate amino transferase, bilirubin), glucose and calcium. The electrolytes become abnormal for many reasons including dehydration and adverse reactions to medications. Kidney malfunction causes the creatinine and blood urea nitrogen to increase. Problems with the liver results in elevations in the liver tests. Diabetes is diagnosed by demonstrating elevated glucose levels.
common_complications: None

name: Clotting studies (blood clot tests)
description: Clotting studies measure the body's ability to clot blood. The most common tests done are the pro-time (PT) and activated partial thromboplastin time (PTT).
common_complications: None

name: Colon biopsy (tissue sample large intestine)
description: A sample of the colon (large intestine) is taken through a colonoscope during a procedure called a colonoscopy. A colonoscope is a long tube with a camera on the end that enables the doctor to see the inside of the colon. The sample is then evaluated to diagnose inflammatory bowel disease, infections, polyps, cancer and other colon diseases.
common_complications: Rectal bleeding, perforation of the colon. Perforation of the colon can cause a serious infection in the abdomen.

name: Coombs test (test for autoimmune cause of anemia)
description: A blood test to identify antibodies that can bind to the surface of red blood cells and destroy them.
common_complications: None

name: Compartment pressure measurement (measures inner muscle pressure)
description: A needle is inserted into a muscle compartment and the pressure in the compartment is measured.
common_complications: Injury to the muscles, nerves, or blood vessels. Infection at the needle insertion site.

name: CSF culture (test for infection in brain fluid)
description: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is the fluid that surrounds the brain and spinal cord. This fluid is cultured to identify bacteria, viruses, and fungi.
common_complications: None

name: CT angiogram of the neck (x-ray images of neck)
description: A computerized tomography (CT) angiogram is a test to see detailed images of the blood vessels of the neck.  The test uses a CT scan and the injection of contrast dye. The study can identify blockages, tears and injury to the arteries of the neck that supply blood to the brain.
common_complications: The contrast dye can injure the kidneys, especially if the person has underlying kidney disease. Some patients can have allergic reactions to the dye, which may be mild or severe.

name: D-Dimer (blood test for blood clots )
description: A D-Dimer is a blood test to help determine if a patient has an active blood clot in a leg or arm vein, or in the lungs. The test can be positive for other reasons besides a blood clot. If the test is positive other tests are generally performed such as an ultrasound of the legs or a CT scan of the chest.
common_complications: None

name: Dexamethasone suppression test (blood test for hormonal abnormality)
description: A blood test that measures the response of the adrenal glands to the synthetic form of cortisol called dexamethasone. A dose of dexamethasone is given at midnight and a blood test cortisol test is done the next morning. Normally the blood cortisol level will be very low after taking dexamethasone. The test is used to help diagnose why a patient has too much cortisol such as in Cushing's disease.
common_complications: None

name: Dix Hallpike maneuver (test for vertigo)
description: An exam performed to help diagnose benign positional vertigo.  The doctor holds the patient's head and asks the patient to lie quickly backward over a table. The doctor will look for abnormal eye movements and ask if the patient feels a spinning sensation.
common_complications: Dizziness, nausea and vomiting

name: Doppler ultrasound (ultrasound for blood vessels)
description: A Doppler ultrasound is a test that can be used to measure blood flow in a vessel by bouncing high-frequency sound waves (ultrasound) off red blood cells in the vessel.
common_complications: None

name: Drug screen
description: A drug screen can be done on urine and/or blood. It is used to detect what drugs a patient has taken. It is most often used to detect illegal drugs like cocaine, PCP, and amphetamines. Its also used to test athletes for use of banned substances.
common_complications: None

name: Endometrial biopsy (uterine biopsy)
description: A procedure in which a tissue sample is taken from the lining of the uterus (endometrium). The sample is examined under a microscope.  It is usually performed to determine the cause of abnormal vaginal bleeding and to rule out endometrial cancer.
common_complications: Pain, injury. Rarely perforation of the uterus occurs.

name: Esophageal manometry (esophageal pressure measurement)
description: A test to measure the pressure inside the lower part of the esophagus. The test determines if the esophagus is contracting and relaxing normally. The study is done to help diagnose swallowing problems and chest pain.
common_complications: Injury including the rare complication of perforation of the esophagus. Most patients are sedated. Rarely someone can have a bad reaction to the anesthesia.

name: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR, blood test for inflammation )
description: ESR (erythrocyte sedimentation rate) is a blood test that often means there is inflammation in the body. It is only a screening test which means that it cannot diagnose a particular disease. If the ESR is high the doctor will perform further testing to find the cause, such as infection, autoimmune disease or other inflammatory disorder.
common_complications: None

name: Fibrin degradation products (blood test for clotting disorder)
description: A blood test for fibrin degradation products. They are the proteins and other microscopic material left behind when clots dissolve in the blood. The blood test is most often used to diagnose a serious abnormality of clotting called DIC (disseminated intravascular coagulation). DIC is most commonly seen in life threatening infections such as sepsis.
common_complications: None

name: Fluorescein staining of cornea (eye)
description: This is a test that uses orange dye (fluorescein) and a blue light (ultraviolet light) to detect scratches, burns, and foreign bodies in the cornea of the eye. The test is most effective when used with a slit lamp.
common_complications: None

name: Follicle stimulating hormone (FSH, female hormone blood test)
description: FSH stands for follicle-stimulating hormone. This hormone is made by the pituitary gland. The FSH level can be measured in the blood. The FSH level rises above normal in menopause. A low FSH level occurs if there is a pituitary problem and may result in problems with sexual development or fertility.
common_complications: None

name: Fungal culture (test to detect fungus)
description: A culture to identify fungus. The culture can be done on blood, sputum, urine, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), and tissue.
common_complications: None

name: Glucose tolerance test (diabetes screening test)
description: The glucose tolerance test is a laboratory test to diagnose diabetes. A patient is given a glucose drink and blood glucose levels are then measured to help diagnose diabetes. It is most often used in patients with mildly elevated fasting blood glucose and in pregnant women at 24-28 weeks to identify gestational diabetes.
common_complications: None

name: Haptoglobin (measure of red blood cell destruction)
description: Haptoglobin is a protein that is produced by the liver. The level can be measured with a simple blood test. Haptoglobin binds free hemoglobin and is helpful in diagnosing the destruction of red blood cells (intravascular hemolytic anemia). When red blood cells are destroyed hemoglobin is released into the blood vessels. This hemoglobin is then bound by haptoglobin causing a decrease in the haptoglobin level.
common_complications: None

name: Hemoglobin A1C (Hb A1C, measures blood glucose over time)
description: HbA1C is a test that determines the amount of glycated hemoglobin in your blood. The level of HbA1C depends upon the average blood sugar level over the prior 2 to 3 months. A high HbA1c indicates blood sugar levels above normal most of the time. The test is done to diagnose diabetes and measure how well a patient's blood glucose level is controlled.
common_complications: None

name: Hepatitis profile (viral hepatitis blood test)
description: Blood tests that measure liver enzymes. Higher amounts of liver enzymes are released from the liver into the blood when the liver is inflamed, infected or injured.
common_complications: None

name: HIDA scan (hepatobiliary iminodiacetic acid scan, gallbladder function test)
description: HIDA scan stands for hepatobiliary iminodiacetic acid scan. It is a test that measures the flow of bile from the liver and gall bladder to the small intestine. The procedure is done to diagnose problems with the bile ducts and gallbladder.
common_complications: None

name: HLA B27 (human leukocyte antigen B27, immune system blood test)
description: HLA-B27 (human leukocyte antigen B27) is a blood test to look for a specific protein found on the surface of white blood cells. Patients that have the HLA B27 protein are more likely to develop certain inflammatory diseases, such as reactive arthritis, sacroiliitis and ankylosing spondylitis.
common_complications: None

name: Holter monitor (portable heart monitor)
description: A Holter monitor is a portable heart monitor that continuously records a patient's heart beat, usually for 24 hours. The device is used to help diagnose abnormal heart rhythms. A patient wears the device with electrodes attached to the chest. The monitor is then taken back to the doctor for analysis.
common_complications: None

name: HSV culture (herpes simplex virus)
description: A culture used to detect the herpes simplex virus, usually taken from an abnormal area on the skin.
common_complications: None

name: Hysteroscopy (camera examination of the uterus)
description: A hysteroscopy is a procedure to look inside the uterus. A small tube with a camera on the end is inserted into the vagina, through the cervix and into the uterus. The instrument may be equipped to allow the doctor to treat minor bleeding, take biopsies and remove small fibroids.
common_complications: Injury to the cervix or uterus causing pain and bleeding. Rarely the uterus can be punctured.

name: Joint fluid analysis (synovial fluid analysis)
description: A needle is inserted into a joint and fluid is removed. The fluid from the joint (synovial fluid) is analyzed for blood cells, bacteria, proteins and crystals. The test is used to diagnose joint infections, gout, certain types of arthritis, and traumatic injuries.
common_complications: Pain and swelling at the needle insertion test site. Rarely infection of the skin or the joint. Injury to a tendon, nerve or blood vessel can rarely occur.

name: Ketones (fat breakdown measurement)
description: Ketones are a byproduct of rapid metabolism of fats in the body. The ketone level can be measured in the urine or the blood. Ketones become elevated in dehydration, starvation and uncontrolled diabetes with ketoacidosis (DKA).
common_complications: None

name: Lactate (blood test for lactic acid)
description: Lactate is produced and released into the blood stream when there is not enough oxygen being delivered to the tissues. This occurs most commonly during sustained intense exercise when the muscles are forced to use anaerobic metabolism. This is a normal reaction by the body. It is also seen in serious diseases where the blood pressure becomes too low such as sepsis. Doctors use a blood lactate level to estimate how well a patient is oxygenating their body.
common_complications: None

name: Luteinizing hormone (LH, pituitary gland hormone measurement)
description: Luteinizing hormone (LH) is a hormone produced by the pituitary gland. An increase in LH at mid-cycle of menses stimulates the ovary to release an egg (ovulate). Doctors most often order a blood LH test to help evaluate infertility or irregular vaginal bleeding.
common_complications: None

name: Lipase (pancreatic blood test)
description: Lipase is an enzyme produced by the pancreas to help digest dietary fats. The lipase blood level increases when the pancreas is damaged or inflamed (pancreatitis).
common_complications: None

name: Lymph node biopsy (remove sample of lymph node)
description: Lymph node biopsy is a test in which a lymph node or a piece of a lymph node is removed for examination under a microscope. Doctors do this test to diagnose cancer,  infection and other diseases.
common_complications: Pain and swelling at the biopsy site. Infection and injury to the surrounding tissues can occur.

name: Mono spot (blood test for mononucleosis)
description: The mononucleosis spot test looks for antibodies in the blood. These are proteins that the bodys immune system produces when a person has mononucleosis caused by the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV).
common_complications: None

name: Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP, MRI image of bile ducts)
description: Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) is a test using a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) machine to evaluate the liver, bile ducts, pancreas and pancreatic ducts.
common_complications: Sometimes the test is performed with a dye called gadolinium. Gadolinium has been associated with a serious skin and connective tissue disease called nephrogenic systemic fibrosis (NSF). Patients with chronic kidney disease are at increased risk of developing NSF after gadolinium. More information can be found at http://www.fda.gov/Drugs/DrugSafety/DrugSafetyNewsletter/ucm142889.

name: Noninvasive vascular assessment (NIVA, ultrasound of blood vessels)
description: A NIVA uses sound waves (ultrasound) to look at the blood vessels and determine if there is normal blood flow or if the vessels contain a blood clot (deep vein thrombosis). The most common place to use a NIVA is on the legs, arms and neck. When done on the leg, it is called a LENI (lower extremity non-invasive).
common_complications: None

name: Vasectomy (surgical male sterilization)
description: A surgical procedure in which the tubes (vas deferens) that carry sperm from the testicles to the penis are cut and blocked. This procedure prevents the sperm from fertilizing the egg during intercourse. The procedure is considered a permanent form of birth control although it can sometimes be reversed with another surgery. The procedure is done in the office under local anesthesia.
common_complications: Patients can experience an infection at the surgical site consisting of redness, increased warmth, or a cloudy discharge from the wound. Bleeding at the site can cause swelling (hematoma) and pain. The large tube (epididymis) next to the sperm carrying tube (vas deferens) can become infected or inflamed. This is called epididymitis. Persistent scrotal discomfort can sometimes occur. Very rarely the procedure can fail and the patient is still able to impregnate his partner.

name: Cholesterol (HDL, LDL, blood fat tests)
description: Cholesterol is a wax-like substance in the body and is necessary for normal body function. Having too much cholesterol can cause fatty deposits in the blood vessels (atherosclerosis) and lead to heart attacks and strokes. The blood test consists of total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, and HDL cholesterol. Having high levels of LDL (bad cholesterol) increases one's risk of atherosclerosis while having high levels of HDL (good cholesterol) is associated with decreased risk.
common_complications: None

name: Cosmetic ear surgery (otoplasty)
description: The most common reasons for performing otoplasty are to reduce the size of large ears, and to pin back ears that protrude too far from the head (ear pinning).
common_complications: Complications include infection, areas of numbness and unsatisfactory results. Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Cosmetic cheek surgery (cheek implant)
description: The most common type of cheek cosmetic surgery is a cheek implant or cheek augmentation. The procedure consists of building up the cheeks with silicone or other material to improve the cosmetic contours of the face.
common_complications: Complications include infection, areas of numbness and unsatisfactory results. If a foreign material is used such as silicone the patient's body can reject the material causing multiple symptoms and excessive scarring. Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Brazilian butt lift (cosmetic buttocks surgery)
description: A particular type of buttocks lift where fat is removed from the thighs and lower back and placed in the buttocks area to produce a more cosmetic contour.
common_complications: Complications include blood clots, infection, areas of numbness and unsatisfactory results. Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Buttocks lift
description: A buttocks lift can be done alone or as part of a total body lift. The procedure is done to improve the contour of the buttocks. The surgeon can remove excess skin and/or add tissue by performing fat injections or an implant. The Brazilian butt lift is a particular buttocks lift.
common_complications: Complications include blood clots, infection, areas of numbness and unsatisfactory results. Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Tympanoplasty (ear drum repair)
description: Tympanoplasty is an eardrum repair. The surgeon repairs a damaged or perforated ear drum and sometimes the adjacent small bones of the middle ear. Typically a graft from a vein or muscle sheath is used, but occasionally an artificial material is required. Infection and trauma are the most common causes of ear drum damage.
