common_complications: Pain during the biopsy and scar formation. There is a small risk of infection. Very rarely surrounding nerves or blood vessels can be damaged.

name: Slit lamp exam (specialized eye exam)
description: An exam using a special instrument to look at the structures in the front part of the eye. This exam is done to detect problems with the eyelids, conjunctiva, cornea, anterior chamber, and lens.
common_complications: None.

name: Corticotropin releasing hormone test (CRH test, blood test)
description: This test helps determine why a patients blood cortisol level is higher than normal. The cortisol level is drawn, then the patient is injected with a dose of synthetic corticotropin releasing hormone (CRH). Next the patient gets a second blood cortisol test. The test is used in difficult to diagnose cases of Cushings disease (over active adrenal glands).
common_complications: None

name: Thyroid scan (image of thyroid using radioactive material)
description: A test to image the thyroid gland in the neck. The patient swallows a small amount of radioactive iodine. The thyroid gland uses iodine to make thyroid hormone. Normal or overactive thyroid tissue takes up the radioactive iodine. The radioactivity is measured using a special camera, which also creates images of the gland. The test is done to evaluate thyroid nodules and to help determine the cause of an elevated thyroid hormone level in the blood (hyperthyroidism).
common_complications: Radiation exposure is low but multiple exposures to radiation may increase cancer risk later in life. This risk is felt to be greater with babies and children.

name: Thyroid blood tests
description: Blood tests used to measure the activity of the thyroid gland and/or the levels of thyroid hormones. The first test usually performed is the thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH). TSH is made by the pituitary gland and it stimulates the release of thyroid hormone from the thyroid gland. A high blood TSH level means a person does not have enough thyroid hormone (hypothyroidism). A low TSH means there is too much thyroid hormone (hyperthyroidism) or the pituitary gland is not making sufficient TSH. Other blood tests can measure the actual amount of thyroid hormone. There are two types in the body, thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3).
common_complications: None.

name: Peritoneal dialysis (blood filtering)
description: A type of dialysis to remove toxins from the blood and correct chemical imbalance in people with kidney failure.  This is an alternative to hemodialysis. A catheter is surgically inserted into the abdominal cavity before starting peritoneal dialysis. At home, the patient runs fluid (dialysate) into and out of the abdominal cavity.  The lining of the abdominal wall (peritoneum) cleans the toxins from the blood and these toxins are removed when the dialysate is removed.
common_complications: Inserting the catheter can cause damage to the abdominal contents. An infection of the abdominal cavity (peritonitis) is the most common complication and can be very serious. Carrying extra fluid in the abdominal cavity can stretch and weaken the abdominal wall.

name: Dialysis catheter insertion
description: In order to receive hemodialysis a patient needs a special catheter to remove blood from the body, to pass through the dialysis machine, and to return the clean blood back to the patient. Both passage ways are contained in the same catheter. These catheters are usually placed in the neck in the internal jugular vein.
common_complications: Damage to the vein or surrounding artery can occur. Collapse of the lung is a rare complication. Infection of the blood stream is a risk as well.

name: Hemodialysis (filter and clean blood)
description: A dialysis procedure that uses a machine to remove toxins from the blood and correct chemical imbalance in people with kidney failure.
common_complications: Infection of the catheter used for dialysis. Low blood pressure during dialysis. Fatigue and weakness for several hours after dialysis.

name: Cortisol (24 hour urine test of hormone level)
description: A 24 hour urine collection sent to the laboratory to measure the total amount of cortisol produced by the adrenal glands. Cortisol is a steroid hormone that is essential for normal functioning of circulation and metabolism. A 24 hour urine collection is needed because cortisol levels fluctuate during the day. The most common reason for the test is to diagnose Cushings disease or other condition that causes excessive cortisol production.
common_complications: None.

name: Audiology test (hearing test)
description: Measures the ability to hear sounds at multiple different tones and intensity. The test is performed to detect early hearing loss from trauma, infections, medications, and chronic exposure to loud noises.
common_complications: None.

name: Spinal fluid analysis
description: Spinal fluid, also known as cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) surrounds the brain and spinal cord. A spinal tap (lumbar puncture) is performed to remove some of this fluid for analysis. The fluid is sent to the laboratory to test for red blood cells, white blood cells, glucose, and protein. The fluid is also cultured to identify any infectious agents. Other tests can also be performed dependent on what disease the provider is trying to detect.
common_complications: None. Complications from the spinal tap include: infection, bleeding, and nerve injury. Another potential problem is leaking of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) causing a spinal headache (postural headache). The pain of a spinal headache decreases with lying flat and increases with standing up.

name: Sputum culture (test for infection in lung mucous)
description: Sputum coughed up from the lung is cultured to identify the organism that may be causing a lung infection (pneumonia). A culture to identify bacteria is the most common type performed but cultures to identify a virus or fungus can also be done.
common_complications: None.

name: Stool culture (test of stool for infection)
description: A test that identifies disease causing organisms in the stool. Bacteria cultures are the most common test performed. There are many types of bacteria that live in human stool that do not cause disease. The most common disease-causing bacteria are salmonella, shigella, campylobacter, Escherichia coli (E. coli) and Clostridium difficile.
common_complications: None.

name: Stool for clostridium difficile (test of stool for bacteria)
description: This test identifies toxins made by the bacteria Clostridium difficile. Clostridium difficile can cause diarrhea. This condition almost always occurs in people that have recently received antibiotics and/or have been hospitalized. The diarrhea can be mild or severe. The severe form is known as pseudomembranous colitis.
common_complications: None.

name: Stool ova and parasite exam (test of stool for parasites)
description: A stool study that looks for parasites or the eggs of parasites. The most common types of parasites are helminths (tapeworms, roundworms and pinworms) and protozoa (giardia, amoeba and cryptosporidium).
common_complications: None

name: Stool WBCs (white blood cells, test of stool for infection)
description: A stool study that looks for white blood cells (WBCs) in the stool. The stool does not normally contain WBCs. When it does, it means there is inflammation (such as colitis) or an infection of the intestine.
common_complications: None.

name: Tuberculosis skin test (PPD skin test)
description: A skin test that measures the immune response to the tuberculosis (TB) bacteria Mycobacterium tuberculosis. A person will have a positive test if they have TB, have been exposed to TB or if they received a vaccine against TB (BCG vaccine). The test is performed by placing a small amount of purified protein derivative (PPD) under the skin. The site is inspected in 48-72 hours by a medical professional who will look for a bump in the skin and measure the size.
common_complications: There is a slight chance of having a very severe skin reaction.

name: Thoracentesis (remove fluid from lung)
description: A procedure done to remove fluid from the space between the lung and the chest wall. Normally this area contains very little fluid. Heart failure, inflammation or infection of the lung lining (called the pleura), trauma and cancer are the most common reasons for fluid to build up in this space. This accumulation of fluid is called a pleural effusion. Removing this fluid can help a patient breath and diagnose the cause of the fluid. The fluid is removed by numbing the overlying skin of the chest and inserting a needle into the chest cavity.
common_complications: Pain at the needle insertion site. Infection and/or a collapse of the lung (pneumothorax) can occur. Rarely a blood vessel, nerve or the lung can be injured.

name: Thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH, blood test to detect thyroid problems)
description: Thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) is blood test used to determine if there is a normal amount of thyroid hormone in the blood. TSH is a protein produced by the pituitary gland. The amount released into the blood stream depends on the level of thyroid hormone in the blood. A high blood TSH level means a person does not have enough thyroid hormone (hypothyroidism). A low TSH means he or she has too much thyroid hormone (hyperthyroidism) or the pituitary gland is not making sufficient TSH.
common_complications: None.

name: Toxicology screen (drug test)
description: There are two basic toxicology screens, one using a urine test and the other a blood test. The urine toxicology screen is used most often. The substances that can be tested on a toxicology screen include: marijuana (tetrahydrocannabinol/THC), opiates, cocaine, amphetamines, benzodiazepines, barbiturates, and phencyclidine (PCP). The substances are cleared from the body at different rates.
common_complications: None.

name: Angiogram, leg (x-ray of lower extremity blood vessels)
description: An angiogram is a procedure that uses x-ray imaging to see the inside of the arteries. An intravenous dye is injected into the artery of the leg and x-rays are taken to view the blood vessel. The test is done to detect blockages of the artery, tears of the artery, and abnormal enlargements of the artery called aneurysms.
common_complications: The artery can be damaged when the needle is inserted into the vessel. The intravenous dye can cause an allergic reaction, which sometimes may be severe. The dye can also injure the kidneys. Patients with pre-existing kidney disease and diabetes are more likely to have kidney damage from the dye.

name: PICC line (long term IV catheter)
description: A PICC line is a special intravenous line inserted into the arm and thread into a blood vessel in the upper chest. A PICC line can be used for longer periods of time as compared to normal intravenous lines placed in the arm. The procedure is done to provide patients with a way to give intravenous therapies over an extended period of time. It's used most often to give patients antibiotics, chemotherapy, or total parental nutrition (TPN).
common_complications: Infection can develop at the insertion site and can involve the catheter itself. Rarely these infections can be serious and involve the blood stream. A blood clot can also develop in the vein.

name: Head CT (CAT scan)
description: A computer enhanced x-ray of the head that provides detailed pictures of the brain and surrounding structures.  The test can be done with or without intravenous dye (contrast). Bleeding in and around the brain can be detected without contrast. But for most other conditions, CT with contrast provides better images.
common_complications: CT scans require radiation. Multiple exposures to radiation increase the risk of cancer later in life. At times intravenous contrast is given with a CT scan. The contrast can injure the kidneys, especially if the person has underlying kidney disease. Some patients can be allergic to the contrast resulting in a rash to life-threatening swelling and low blood pressure.

name: Chest CT (CAT) scan with dye
description: A computer enhanced x-ray of the chest that provides detailed pictures of the lungs and other structures in the chest. The intravenous dye (contrast) is used to detect blood clots (pulmonary embolus), after traumatic injuries to identify blood vessel damage, and to better define other problems in the chest. High resolution CT scans can see the blood vessels of the heart (coronary arteries) and estimate the amount of blockage of these arteries.
common_complications: CT scans require radiation. Multiple exposures to radiation increase the risk of cancer later in life. At times intravenous contrast is given with a CT scan. The contrast can injure the kidneys, especially if the person has underlying kidney disease. Some patients can be allergic to the contrast resulting in a rash to life-threatening swelling and low blood pressure.

name: Chest CT (CAT) scan without dye
description: A computer enhanced x-ray of the chest that provides detailed pictures of the lungs and other structures in the chest. When used without intravenous dye (contrast), the test is usually done to identify cancers, infections, and abnormal fluid collections around the lungs (pleural effusions) or around the heart (pericardial effusions).
common_complications: CT scans require radiation. Multiple exposures to radiation increase the risk of cancer later in life.

name: Abdominal pelvic CT (CAT) scan without intravenous dye
description: A computer enhanced x-ray of the abdomen and pelvis that provides detailed pictures of the internal organs and other structures in and around the abdomen and pelvis. This test helps detect abnormalities of the liver, spleen, pancreas, kidneys, uterus, ovaries, bladder, stomach and intestines. Usually, oral contrast is given before the test. But intravenous dye is not given with this test.
common_complications: CT scans require radiation. Multiple exposures to radiation increase the risk of cancer later in life.

name: Abdominal pelvic CT (CAT) scan with dye
description: A computer enhanced x-ray of the abdomen and pelvis that provides detailed pictures of the internal organs and other structures in and around the abdomen and pelvis. This test can identify abnormalities of the appendix, liver, spleen, pancreas, kidneys, uterus, ovaries, bladder, stomach and intestines. Intravenous dye (contrast) is used to obtain better images of the blood vessels and internal organs.
common_complications: CT scans require radiation. Multiple exposures to radiation increase the risk of cancer later in life. At times intravenous contrast is given with a CT scan. The contrast can injure the kidneys, especially if the person has underlying kidney disease. Some patients can be allergic to the contrast resulting in a rash to life-threatening swelling and low blood pressure.

name: Facial CT (CAT) scan without dye
description: A computer enhanced x-ray that provides detailed images of the face, jaw, and facial bones. This procedure is performed to identify fractures, infections, cancers, and congenital abnormalities.
common_complications: CT scans require radiation. Multiple exposures to radiation increase the risk of cancer later in life.

name: Brain MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) with and without dye
description: MRI is magnetic resonance imaging, a special imaging test that does not use x-rays. This test provides very detailed images of the brain, structures of the face, and sinuses. In general a MRI is better at determining acute strokes, infections and cancers than a CT scan. An intravenous dye called gadolinium is sometimes used to obtain better images.
common_complications: Gadolinium has been associated with a serious skin and connective tissue disease called nephrogenic systemic fibrosis (NSF). Patients with chronic kidney disease are at increased risk of developing NSF after gadolinium. More information can be found at http://www.fda.gov/Drugs/DrugSafety/DrugSafetyNewsletter/ucm142889.htm.

name: Neck MRI without dye
description: MRI is magnetic resonance imaging, a special imaging test that does not use x-rays. This test provides very detailed images of the neck muscles, ligaments, nerves, bones, and soft tissue. This test is used to identify traumatic injuries, infections, and cancer.
common_complications: None

name: Back MRI without dye
description: MRI is magnetic resonance imaging, a special imaging test that does not use x-rays. This test provides very detailed images of the back and spinal cord. This procedure can help identify arthritis, cancers, infections, fractures, injured nerves, a damaged spinal cord or a herniated disc.
common_complications: None

name: Lower extremity joint MRI without dye (leg MRI)
description: MRI is magnetic resonance imaging, a special imaging test that does not use x-rays. This test provides very detailed images of the joint and surrounding muscles and bones. This procedure can help identify arthritis, traumatic injuries, ligament tears, tendon ruptures, meniscus injuries, infections and fractures.
common_complications: None

name: Breast ultrasound
description: A diagnostic imaging test. The ultrasound device is pressed against the breast, and sound waves from the device bounce off tissues and create echoes. The pictures can determine if a breast mass is solid or cystic. Simple cysts are almost always benign. A solid mass may be benign or malignant.
common_complications: None.

name: Pelvic ultrasound
description: A diagnostic imaging test. The ultrasound device is pressed against the lower abdomen, and sound waves from the device bounce off tissues and create echoes. Pelvic ultrasounds are routinely performed during pregnancy.  Pelvic ultrasound is also used to get pictures of pelvic organs, including the bladder, the uterus and ovaries in a woman, and the prostate in a man. This test can help identify cysts, free fluid in the pelvis, changes consistent with infection, ectopic pregnancy and abnormal growths.
common_complications: None.

name: Rubella titer (German measles blood test)
description: A test that looks for antibodies against the rubella (German measles) virus. This test is used to identify if someone has immunity against rubella either from a vaccine or a prior infection. The test can also help determine if someone is currently infected or has recently been infected with rubella.
common_complications: None.

name: Diphtheria, tetanus and pertussis vaccine (DTaP, Tdap and Td)
description: A vaccine that protects against diphtheria, tetanus and pertussis. There are two types of the vaccines that are used: DTaP and Tdap. Children should get DTaP vaccine at 2 months, 4 months, 6 months, 15-18 months, and 4-6 years. DTaP is given to children less than 7 years of age and Tdap is used for people older than age 11. The CDC recommends a Tdap booster at age 11 or 12. Also a Tdap booster should be given during every pregnancy, preferably in the third trimester. Adults will also need a Td (tetanus and diphtheria) booster every ten years after their Tdap vaccine. The following people should not receive the vaccine: people with a history of a severe allergic reaction after the vaccine; and those who have experienced a coma or multiple seizures within 7 days of receiving the vaccine. Any patient with a history of seizures, other nervous system diseases, a history of Guillain Barre, or are ill at the time of the vaccination should talk to their healthcare provider before receiving this vaccine.
common_complications: The CDC believes becoming infected and developing diphtheria, tetanus or pertussis poses a much greater risk to people compared to the risk of a side effect from the vaccine. Serious reactions are rare. For more information see http://www.cdc.gov/vaccines/hcp/vis/vis-statements/dtap.html

name: Measles, mumps, rubella vaccine (MMR)
description: A vaccine that protects against mumps, measles and rubella. Children should receive this vaccine between 12-15 months and at 4-6 years of age. Adults should get the vaccine if they were born after 1956 and if they are not sure if they have been vaccinated or if they only received one vaccine before entering school. The MMR vaccine may be given at the same time as other vaccines. The following patients should not receive the vaccine: those with a history of a severe allergic reaction to the vaccine; those with a severe allergic reaction to gelatin or the antibiotic neomycin; those with HIV or any other disease that depresses the immune system; those receiving medications that depress the immune system including 2 weeks or more of high dose steroids; and those with cancer or being treated for cancer. The patients with the following should talk to their healthcare provider before receiving the vaccine: a history or family history of seizures; a family history of immune system diseases; a history of diseases of the blood including a low platelet count; recent history of a blood transfusion; or those who might be pregnant.
common_complications: The CDC believes becoming infected and developing mumps, measles or rubella poses a much greater risk to people compared to the risk of a side effect from the vaccine. Serious complications are rare. There is no association between MMR and autism.

name: Breast biopsy (breast tissue removal)
description: A breast biopsy involves removing some breast tissue either through an incision or by using a needle. This procedure is performed to diagnose the cause of a breast mass or other breast abnormality.
common_complications: Pain and scar formation. There is a small risk of infection. Rarely surrounding nerves or blood vessels can be damaged.

name: Inguinal hernia repair (groin hernia surgery)
description: A surgical procedure to repair a defect in the abdominal wall surrounding the inguinal canal. People with this type of hernia have intestines or other abdominal contents that push into and through the inguinal canal. This is the most common type of hernia in men. The repair can often be done with a laparoscope.
common_complications: Any surgery can result in infection, pain, and the development of blood clots in the legs or lungs after surgery. Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Laparoscopic vaginal hysterectomy (minimally invasive uterus removal)
description: Surgical removal of the uterus through the vagina with laparoscopic assistance. A laparoscope is a special tube with a camera that is inserted into the abdomen through a small incision in the abdomen.
common_complications: Injury to intestines, ovaries, bladder, or pelvic vessels. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Uterine fibroid removal (surgical removal of uterine growths)
description: Surgical removal of fibroids in the uterus. Depending on the size of the fibroid(s), the procedure is performed with a laparoscope using small incisions or through a larger incision in the abdomen. Fibroids are noncancerous overgrowths of muscular and fibrous tissue of the uterus.
common_complications: Injury to intestines, ovaries, bladder, or pelvic vessels. The surgery can result in post-operative pain, infection or blood clots of the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolus). Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Tympanometry (ear drum testing)
description: Measures how well the eardrum (tympanic membrane) moves. A tool is inserted into the ear that delivers a puff of air to measure the eardrum movement. Fluid behind the eardrum can prevent the eardrum from moving normally. An infection (otitis media) or a malfunctioning eustachian tube can cause abnormal fluid build-up. A hole in the eardrum can also cause abnormal movement of the eardrum.
common_complications: Very rarely the eardrum can be damaged.

name: Knee arthroscopy (camera knee joint examination)
description: A tube with a camera is inserted into the knee joint to identify any damage to the bone, cartilage, meniscus, ligaments or joint capsule. Many times the repair of the damaged tissue can be performed at the same time. This procedure can be done under general anesthesia or regional anesthesia.
common_complications: Complications include injury to the joint, ligaments, cartilage, nerves or blood vessels. All surgery comes with the risk of infection and blood clots. Patients can infrequently have bad reactions to anesthesia.

name: Hep lock (saline lock, IV catheter)
description: An attachment to an intravenous (IV) catheter that contains saline or a blood thinning agent called heparin. It prevents the IV catheter from clotting when its not being used.
common_complications: Pain from the needle or catheter that remains in place. Infection or the development of a blood clot in the vein occurs very rarely.

name: Lumbar MRI without dye (lower back MRI)
description: MRI is magnetic resonance imaging, a special imaging test that does not use x-rays. A MRI of the lower back can identify ligaments, muscles, nerves, discs, bones, and the spinal cord. It is the best test to detect arthritis, herniated discs, spinal infections, spinal cord damage, nerve injuries, and cancers of the back and spinal cord.
common_complications: None.

name: Cervical spine MRI without dye (neck MRI)
description: MRI is magnetic resonance imaging, a special imaging test that does not use x-rays. The bones of the neck make up the cervical spine. A MRI of the cervical spine can identify ligaments, muscles, nerves, discs, bones, and the spinal cord. It is the best test to detect arthritis, herniated discs, spinal infections, spinal cord damage, nerve injuries, and cancers of the spinal cord.
common_complications: None.

name: Thoracic spine MRI without dye (upper back MRI)
description: MRI is magnetic resonance imaging, a special imaging test that does not use x-rays. The bones of the middle back make up the thoracic spine. A MRI of the thoracic spine can identify ligaments, muscles, nerves, discs, bones, and the spinal cord. It is the best test to detect arthritis, herniated discs, spinal infections, spinal cord damage, nerve injuries, and cancers of the spinal cord.
common_complications: None.

name: Lumbar MRI with dye (lower back MRI)
description: MRI is magnetic resonance imaging, a special imaging test that does not use x-rays. A MRI of the lower back can identify ligaments, muscles, nerves, discs, bones, and the spinal cord. It is the best test to detect arthritis, herniated discs, spinal infections, spinal cord damage, nerve injuries, and cancers of the back and spinal cord. A dye named gadolinium is used to provide more detailed pictures. This can help detect the difference between inflammation, traumatic injury or cancer.
common_complications: Gadolinium has been associated with a serious skin and connective tissue disease called nephrogenic systemic fibrosis (NSF). It appears patients with chronic kidney disease are at increased risk of developing NSF after gadolinium. More information can be found at http://www.fda.gov/Drugs/DrugSafety/DrugSafetyNewsletter/ucm142889.htm

name: Cervical spine MRI with dye (neck MRI)

name: Lumbar CT scan without dye (lower back CAT scan)
description: A test using computer enhanced x-rays that provides detailed images of the bones (lumbar spine) and spinal cord in the lower back. This test can help diagnose fractures, infections, arthritis, cancers, herniated discs, and lumbar spinal stenosis.
common_complications: CT scans require radiation. Multiple exposures to radiation increase the risk of cancer later in life.

name: Lumbar CT scan with dye (lower back CAT scan)
description: A test using computer enhanced x-rays that provides detailed images of the bones (lumbar spine) and spinal cord in the lower back.  Dye (contrast) is given in the vein to provide better images of the blood vessels and other structures. This test can identify fractures, infections, arthritis, cancers, herniated discs, spinal stenosis, spinal cord injuries, and nerve damage of the lower back.
common_complications: CT scans require radiation. Multiple exposures to radiation increase the risk of cancer later in life. The intravenous contrast dye can injure the kidneys, especially if the person has underlying kidney disease. Some patients can be allergic to the contrast resulting in a rash to life-threatening swelling and low blood pressure.

name: Cervical spine CT without dye (neck CAT scan)
description: A test using computer enhanced x-rays that provides detailed images of the bones (cervical spine) and spinal cord in the neck.  This test can help diagnose fractures, infections, arthritis, cancers, herniated discs, and cervical spinal stenosis.
common_complications: CT scans require radiation. Multiple exposures to radiation increase the risk of cancer later in life.

name: Cervical spine CT with dye (neck CAT scan)
description: A test using computer enhanced x-rays that provides detailed images of the bones (cervical spine) and spinal cord. Dye (contrast) is given in the vein to provide better images of the blood vessels and other structures. This test can identify fractures, infections, arthritis, cancers, herniated discs, spinal stenosis, spinal cord injuries, and nerve damage of the neck.
common_complications: CT scans require radiation. Multiple exposures to radiation increase the risk of cancer later in life. The intravenous contrast can injure the kidneys, especially if the person has underlying kidney disease. Some patients can be allergic to the contrast resulting in a rash to life-threatening swelling and low blood pressure.

description: A test using computer enhanced x-rays that provides detailed images of the bones (thoracic spine) and spinal cord in the middle back. This test can help diagnose fractures, infections, arthritis, cancers, and herniated discs.
common_complications: CT scans require radiation. Multiple exposures to radiation increase the risk of cancer later in life.

description: A test using computer enhanced x-rays that provides detailed images of the bones (thoracic spine) and spinal cord in the middle back.
